Where the original or the later curvature is the same in every direction the property depends on, the two retained fractions are equal at every τ\tau; where both curvatures are λ\lambda times the identity, both fractions are e−λτe^{-\lambda\tau}, 0.368 at λτ=1\lambda\tau = 1, and the model gives no advantage at all. P23 predicts more: an advantage of at least 0.10 at the matched budget, decided only under later training of the same kind as the capability formation, which its deciding unit records as the same loss on data of the same domain (registration version 1.105, P23, its third fixed thing and the later training’s kind). That margin is the registration’s declared convention, “not derived from the framework”, so P23 is an empirical prediction and no result of this section proves it. The registration gives Assumption S and Theorem IV-C as its reason for that narrowing, and both stay unregistered.

Coupling.

Let the later objective depend on the property: the later loss plus 12γ(V(ω)−Vtgt)2\tfrac{1}{2}\gamma\,(V(\omega) - V_{\mathrm{tgt}})^2, with γ>0\gamma > 0, so that a departure of the property from its target value costs performance. Write stf:=1/(g⊤Φ+g)\mathrm{stf} := 1/(g^\top\Phi^{+} g) where gg lies in the range of Φ\Phi, with Φ+\Phi^{+} its pseudo-inverse, and stf:=0\mathrm{stf} := 0 where gg has a component in the null space of Φ\Phi: the least capability cost, at second order, of lowering VV by a given amount from the later minimum is 12stf\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{stf} times the amount’s square.

Proposition IV-U (coupling; the report’s own models, not registered). For every γ>0\gamma > 0: (1) from the coupled objective’s minimum, the least increase of that objective that lowers VV by a given amount is 12(stf+γ)\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{stf} + \gamma) times the amount’s square; (2) at that minimum the property’s distance from its target is (V(ω⋆)−Vtgt)stf/(stf+γ)(V(\omega^\star) - V_{\mathrm{tgt}})\,\mathrm{stf}/(\mathrm{stf} + \gamma), which is zero where gg has a component in the null space of Φ\Phi; (3) under further training on the coupled objective every departure of the property from its value at that minimum decays to zero, whatever direction made it, whereas without coupling a departure made in a flat direction stays. (Proof: Appendix A.11.)

Part (3) is, in a model, what Creating Friendly AI (Yudkowsky 2001) says in words of a feature a system would itself produce: “Perturb the design, and the design will swiftly return to the norm.” (section 5.3.2, page 102). There the return comes from the system’s own goals (“Every feature needs to correspond to a subgoal in order to go on existing.”, the same page); here it comes from a coupling term in a training objective applied by gradient flow. So in the model a property can last because little pushes on it, which is what joint installation buys, or because the objective that drives further change pulls it back, which is what coupling buys. Only the second restores the property after a one-off displacement, and only while the later objective keeps the coupling term; a strong weight decay moves the equilibrium towards the decay’s reference. Under coupling the baseline run acquires the property too, and the caution of Section 5.6 applies: the concurrent-baseline retained fraction tends to zero while the property is held.

Limitations and standing.

The training model is local and quadratic, with one fixed curvature and an affine property score; each is contested for real networks. It is offered for the conditions it names and the measurements it suggests, never as evidence, and it supports no verdict on P15 or on P23. Theorem IV-S is standard (Section 2); Proposition IV-L’s costs are standard in substance; Theorem IV-C and Corollary IV-C′' are proved here. A search of 14 November 2026 (twenty sources read at source, the nearest empirical study read in full) and a reading of 17 November 2026 of one earlier theory of curvature-driven decay of safety did not find this comparison stated; Section 2 says what those two works state.

6 Law V, the ARC Embedding Law

6.1 Statement

Law V, the ARC Embedding Law (added 24 September 2026; registered as a law on 15 October 2026 by version 1.103; a law under test, Section 11) concerns the genesis strategy (register ARC-5) and carries P12, whether build order moves the correction-leverage exponent, and P21, whether correction placed inside the loop pulls away from correction applied outside it as depth grows. The registration (Eastwood 2026j) states it in two limbs, opening “Where correction sits is an intervention point rather than an accident of history.” Its build-order limb reads: “a corrector formed before the capability it corrects has a correction-leverage exponent larger, by at least the registered minimum effect, than a corrector added after it, at matched content”; its placement limb is P21’s registered claim, word for word (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, its statement in two limbs). Two limbs, separate hypotheses with no shared mechanism assumed:

  • Placement limb. Its registered face is P21, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1219): “Correction that participates in each subsequent revision round outperforms correction that sees only the finished output, and the advantage widens as recursive depth rises rather than staying constant.” P21 decides an access and action-space interaction on the outcome, “never a measurement of an exponent” (registration version 1.102, line 1221). The registration makes the limb P21’s own verdict, scored under P21’s entry with the two readings it adds there: a directional reading, under which no widening of the registered size, or a narrowing, is scored against P21; and a mechanism axis, whether the monitor’s detection rate falls as the artefact it inspects grows and how much of the widening that fall can carry, printed beside P21’s mark and never in its place. A limb supported while that axis is unsupported, inconclusive or NOT EVALUABLE is printed as supported on the performance axis only, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the placement limb, and P21, the directional reading and the two verdicts). That mechanism axis is not the mechanism reading that follows. The registration’s own mechanism reading is written in its own quantities (registration version 1.102, line 1239): “that correction embedded in the recursion carries a larger direct depth-dependence than correction applied from outside it. Where that holds, the boundary rises with it”. In this document’s symbols the mechanism reading is ηo,in>ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} > \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}} at matched order oo. It is carried here as the registered mechanism reading, which no verdict in this document decides: a P21 verdict does not measure it, and its refutation does not prove ηo,in≤ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} \le \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}}.

  • Build-order limb. Its registered face is P12, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1033): “The order in which a system’s components are built changes its correction-leverage exponent by at least the registered minimum effect.” The contrast is the registered maximal contrast (registration version 1.102, line 1037): “a corrector formed before the capability it corrects against a corrector added after it, at matched content”; the minimum effect is 0.10 on the correction-leverage exponent scale (registration version 1.102, line 1041); in this document’s symbols the endpoint is χfirst−χafter\chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}} at the placement the instrument fixes, named in the report (P12 registers no placement factor), read on the target axis under Section 4’s identification conditions, and on one fault set of stated type, the same for both orders: the registration measures the exponent “on a fixed fault set of stated type” (registration version 1.102, line 389), and it sets P12 beside P22 on the same quantity by different routes, “P22 says that elasticity differs with the type of fault corrected, and this says it moves with the order in which the corrector was built”, adding “The two are severable and neither carries the other.” (registration version 1.102, line 1045). P22 stays in ARC-3 (registration version 1.102, line 99) and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, does not carry it, and a build-order contrast read across a changed mix of fault types would carry part of the ordering P22 registers, and could reach the minimum effect with no effect of order at all. P12 registers no direction and is given none here. Version 1.103 registers the build-order limb with a direction P12 does not carry, read on P12’s interval and printed beside P12’s mark, never in its place (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the build-order limb). In this document’s symbols the limb’s claim is the genesis reading, that formation first carries the higher elasticity by at least the registered minimum effect, χfirst−χafter≥0.10\begin{equation*} \chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}} \ge 0.10 \end{equation*}(9) at the placement the instrument fixes (or at least the smaller minimum a future instrument registers, registration version 1.102, line 1041); earlier versions of this document stated it as a reading beside P12 and not as law content, and version 1.103 registers it as the limb (Section 9). The margin is the minimum-effect convention, and it stands in the reading’s statement as well as in its strike rule, because only so is the reading consistent with P12’s undirected registration: a reading that formation first exceeds formation after by a margin implies P12’s claim exactly when that margin is at least P12’s registered minimum, and with a smaller margin, or none, it can hold at every point of an interval on which P12’s registered refuter fires. So stated, the reading is the upward half of P12’s claim, adds a sign and nothing else, and never counts as its support a change P12’s registration reports “as no effect of interest rather than as no effect” (registration version 1.102, line 1041). In the smallest model stated here (Section 6.8), a corrector formed first out-scales one added after only where its coverage of the target’s faults decays, as capability is formed after it, more slowly than a corrector added after falls behind a target it must learn with matched content. With no co-scaling and a decay at least as fast as the target’s representation grows, the limb’s direction reverses. The limb therefore carries a premise about the persistence of what is formed first, which is the question of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, asked of the corrector.

Boundary reading (conditional).

Where a limb raises ηol\eta_{ol} with κ>χ\kappa > \chi, or raises χol\chi_{ol} with η>ζ\eta > \zeta, the burden elasticities being fixed, the balance boundary of Section 7 rises, for changes small enough, or large changes that keep κ−χ\kappa - \chi of one sign; a change of χ\chi across κ\kappa turns a ceiling into a floor (Proposition B-2) (registration version 1.102, line 1045: “Where it moves upward the boundary rises with it.”; the domains are those of Proposition B-6). The reading depends on the ARC Ceiling’s model and, through it, on ARC-2; it is not a verdict rule, and no boundary measurement scores a limb (Section 8).

6.2 Quantities, embedding defined operationally, and the prerequisite

Quantities.

On a declared domain C>0C > 0, R>0R > 0, each arm’s correction service Qol(C,R)Q_{ol}(C, R) is positive and differentiable with other design factors fixed; capability CC carries the ratio scale Condition B fixes, justified independently of the framework and fixed before any outcome (registration version 1.102, line 403), on which every exponent number in this document is stated (Section 7.7); RR is the modelled depth where registration version 1.102, line 263 applies. Zero service is reported outside the log model and never replaced by an outcome-chosen offset (registration version 1.102, line 265, applied to service); because excluding zeros conditions on the outcome, the zero counts are reported per cell, and a two-part or censored model stands among the rivals of Section 6.4. The local elasticities χol\chi_{ol} and ηol\eta_{ol} are partial derivatives of ln⁡Qol\ln Q_{ol}; the constant-elasticity case is the power law and returns the programme’s exponents (Proposition V-3). The local reading is the author’s: his working paper of 16 August 2026 (Eastwood 2026a) defines κ\kappa, ζ\zeta, χ\chi and η\eta as local partial elasticities of W(C,r)W(C, r) and Q(C,r)Q(C, r), and the registration reads the growth exponent the same way (registration version 1.102, line 267: “the elasticity of capability in depth, taken at the depth a system has reached”, with the fitted slope “the special case in which that elasticity is constant”). Identification with the registered correction-leverage exponent needs the conditions of Section 4; otherwise χol\chi_{ol} is the elasticity of the declared service measure. ηol\eta_{ol} is the direct depth-dependence of correction service and is not an integration fraction.

Embedding, defined operationally.

Writing the next state as a function of the current state and a correction term, against applying a correction to the finished next state, does not by itself distinguish embedded from external correction: the second form also determines the next state and can be written as one transition map. What can be registered is operational: the treatment schedule (whether correction enters the next round or only inspects its output), the information available to the corrector, the action space (accept or reject only, against generation under constraint), and whether correction feeds later revisions. P21’s deciding unit fixes exactly these (registration version 1.102, line 1231: three regimes crossed with depth, matched on model, calls and token budget, manipulating information access; registration version 1.102, line 1233: the action space also differs, and the per-round rejection rate is reported beside the interaction). Matching away information access would be a new mechanism-isolating comparison, not an amendment to P21.

The recursive-improvement condition.

It is stated here (the report’s own models; not registered) as a prerequisite beneath all five laws, in words: the outputs of one round must causally change a later improvement transition. It is not a law; it would be a condition of the laws only if the author registers it, and until then it is a description that no surface states as a condition of any law, Laws I to III, each a law under test, included; no symbol is given to it here. Two operational forms have been put forward, both positivity conditions on a mutual information, and both are declined as criteria. Both are written elsewhere with the updater’s letter, one of the eight colliding symbols of Section 4, so they are described here in words. The state-based form asks that the mutual information between successive states, conditional on the updater’s current state, be positive; it is met by pure repetition. The update-based form asks that the mutual information between the updater’s next state and the two successive states, conditional on the updater’s current state, be positive; it separates repetition from update, but a prerequisite is a necessary condition, and this form is not necessary: a deterministic recursion from a fixed initial state, in which every state and every update are fixed functions of their predecessors, has zero entropy everywhere and so zero mutual information, yet its outputs causally change each later transition. The fixed initial state is needed, and it is a valid instance: from a uniformly random initial state the same kind of recursion can carry positive information, one bit when that state is a single uniformly random bit. Mutual information measures statistical dependence, not the causal change the prerequisite names; neither form is an improvement criterion either, since information can persist unchanged or guide a harmful update.

6.3 Identities and the one-path counterexample

Identity V-1 (the embedding ratio’s log-derivatives).

At matched order, Gemb:=Qin/QoutG_{\mathrm{emb}} := Q_{\mathrm{in}}/Q_{\mathrm{out}}. At fixed CC: dln⁡Gemb/dln⁡R=ηin−ηout\mathrm{d}\ln G_{\mathrm{emb}}/\mathrm{d}\ln R = \eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}}. At fixed RR: dln⁡Gemb/dln⁡C=χin−χout\mathrm{d}\ln G_{\mathrm{emb}}/\mathrm{d}\ln C = \chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}. Along a common path C(R)C(R) with αR=dln⁡C/dln⁡R\alpha_R = \mathrm{d}\ln C/\mathrm{d}\ln R: dln⁡Gemb/dln⁡R=αR(χin−χout)+(ηin−ηout).\begin{equation*} \mathrm{d}\ln G_{\mathrm{emb}}/\mathrm{d}\ln R = \alpha_R(\chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}) + (\eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}}). \end{equation*}(10) Proof: ln⁡Gemb=ln⁡Qin−ln⁡Qout\ln G_{\mathrm{emb}} = \ln Q_{\mathrm{in}} - \ln Q_{\mathrm{out}}; the partials are the definitions; the total derivative is the chain rule. So the path derivative is not in general ηin−ηout\eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}}: that equality holds at fixed CC and, along a path, only where αR(χin−χout)=0\alpha_R(\chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}) = 0, that is where capability is not moving along the path or the two arms’ capability elasticities agree.

Identity V-2 (separate arm paths).

Where the arms run on their own trajectories Cin(R)C_{\mathrm{in}}(R) and Cout(R)C_{\mathrm{out}}(R), with αin:=dln⁡Cin/dln⁡R\alpha_{\mathrm{in}} := \mathrm{d}\ln C_{\mathrm{in}}/\mathrm{d}\ln R and αout:=dln⁡Cout/dln⁡R\alpha_{\mathrm{out}} := \mathrm{d}\ln C_{\mathrm{out}}/\mathrm{d}\ln R, the depth derivative of the log-ratio is αinχin+ηin−αoutχout−ηout\alpha_{\mathrm{in}}\chi_{\mathrm{in}} + \eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \alpha_{\mathrm{out}}\chi_{\mathrm{out}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}}, each term on its own path; further varying factors add their own chain-rule terms.

Counterexample to one-path identification.

Qin=C2Q_{\mathrm{in}} = C^2, Qout=CQ_{\mathrm{out}} = C on the path C=RC = R: the ratio equals RR and widens, dln⁡Gemb/dln⁡R=1\mathrm{d}\ln G_{\mathrm{emb}}/\mathrm{d}\ln R = 1, while ηin−ηout=0\eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}} = 0; the widening is αR(χin−χout)=1\alpha_R(\chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}) = 1. One path therefore does not identify the partials; crossed or off-path variation is needed (registration version 1.102, line 621), and no power law is needed for the chain rule itself.

Proposition V-3 (constant elasticities). If χol\chi_{ol} and ηol\eta_{ol} are constant on a rectangle of the (ln⁡C,ln⁡R)(\ln C, \ln R) plane containing the reference point (C0,R0)(C_0, R_0), then on it ln⁡(Qol/Q0)=ln⁡(Qol,0/Q0)+χolln⁡(C/C0)+ηolln⁡(R/R0),\begin{equation*} \ln(Q_{ol}/Q_0) = \ln(Q_{ol,0}/Q_0) + \chi_{ol}\ln(C/C_0) + \eta_{ol}\ln(R/R_0), \end{equation*}(11) and at matched order Gemb=G0(C/C0)χin−χout(R/R0)ηin−ηout.\begin{equation*} G_{\mathrm{emb}} = G_0\,(C/C_0)^{\chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}}\,(R/R_0)^{\eta_{\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{\mathrm{out}}}. \end{equation*}(12) (Proof: Appendix A.12.)

This is the reduced scaling form: earned where the elasticities are constant, assumed nowhere.

6.4 The estimable model (the report’s own models; not registered)

For cell (o,l)(o, l), family and task, a candidate mixed model is ln⁡(Q/Q0)=ln⁡(Qol,0/Q0)+χolln⁡(C/C0)+ηolln⁡(R/R0)+u0,family+uC,familyln⁡(C/C0)+uR,familyln⁡(R/R0)+u0,task+uC,taskln⁡(C/C0)+uR,taskln⁡(R/R0)+ψ,\begin{equation*} \begin{multlined} \ln(Q/Q_0) = \ln(Q_{ol,0}/Q_0) + \chi_{ol}\ln(C/C_0) + \eta_{ol}\ln(R/R_0) \\ + u_{0,\mathrm{family}} + u_{C,\mathrm{family}}\ln(C/C_0) + u_{R,\mathrm{family}}\ln(R/R_0) \\ + u_{0,\mathrm{task}} + u_{C,\mathrm{task}}\ln(C/C_0) + u_{R,\mathrm{task}}\ln(R/R_0) + \psi,\end{multlined} \end{equation*}(13) with random intercepts and random slopes by family and by task, their covariance structure fixed before any outcome, and the residual ψ\psi. Where the design crosses arms within a family or a task, the random effects also carry the arm terms (the indicators and their slope interactions), because otherwise the standard errors of the very contrasts the kill conditions read are understated. The fixed part is saturated in the 2×22 \times 2 cells: four intercepts, four capability slopes, four depth slopes. Equivalently, each of the three coefficient types is written with the indicators indfirst\mathrm{ind}_{\mathrm{first}}, indin\mathrm{ind}_{\mathrm{in}} and their product, and the two parametrisations are the same twelve parameters, since the cell design has rank four. A model with random intercepts only whose fixed part keeps six of these twelve terms (the common intercept, the intercept on the product of the two indicators, the common slopes on ln⁡C\ln C and on ln⁡R\ln R, the order×ln⁡C{}\times\ln C slope and the placement×ln⁡R{}\times\ln R slope) omits the other six: the two indicator main effects, the placement×ln⁡C{}\times\ln C and order×ln⁡R{}\times\ln R slopes and the two three-way slope terms. The order contrast at placement ll is χfirst,l−χafter,l\chi_{\mathrm{first},l} - \chi_{\mathrm{after},l}, which depends on ll unless the three-way capability-slope term is zero, so the contrast is always reported at a named placement; the placement contrast at order oo is ηo,in−ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} - \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}}. Whether model family enters as a random factor or as a fixed stratum is ruled once, before any data. A random factor needs a population of which the families are a sample, named in the registration, and a design with a handful of families from a few providers has none; such a design treats each family as a fixed stratum, with the family terms above as fixed effects, prints each family’s contrast and pools the families with weights fixed in advance, as Unit 83b, the counted test of in-loop correction with depth on three providers, pools its engines with equal weight and prints each engine’s own estimate. The task terms are unchanged.

Estimands and controls.

Any estimate of χ\chi entering a P12 verdict is the estimate registration version 1.102, line 387 requires: a slope of one measured quantity on another carries error on both axes, the ratio of those errors is registered before any fitting, “the attenuation-corrected estimate is the one that enters a verdict”, and no cell contributes an exponent unless it clears the identifiability gate of “at least four valid measurement intervals and at least one and a half decades of administered depth”. Crossed or off-path variation in CC and RR is needed to identify the partials (registration version 1.102, line 621). Exposure, correction compute and information access are design controls: conditioning on them defines a resource-normalised contrast and changes the estimand; P21’s registered face is on its own registered access manipulation (registration version 1.102, line 1231), so a matched-access design is a different comparison (Section 6.2). Capability is treated in the same way wherever an arm can move it: where the placement or the build order changes the capability the system attains, a comparison at fixed CC conditions on a quantity the arm moves, so it is a controlled contrast, read as an effect of the arm only under assumptions stated before any outcome, and the total effect, the log-ratio of the two arms’ service each along its own path, whose depth trend Identity V-2 gives, is reported beside it; administered capability, or target difficulty varied independently of the arm, is the preferred design factor where it can be had. The two estimands can differ in either direction. With the capability elasticity of service constant at χ\chi: identical service surfaces give a zero contrast at every fixed CC, while an arm that raises attained capability by a factor that grows with depth has a total effect of χ\chi times the logarithm of that factor, which widens with depth where χ\chi is positive; and an arm that doubles service at fixed CC while halving attained capability has a contrast of ln⁡2\ln 2 at every fixed CC and a total effect of (1−χ)ln⁡2(1 - \chi)\ln 2, which is zero at χ=1\chi = 1 and takes the opposite sign to the contrast where χ\chi exceeds one. The slopes themselves are read the same way. Where ln⁡(C/C0)\ln(C/C_0) is attained capability rather than capability the design assigns, any latent factor that moves both capability and correction service enters the slope: in a linear model with the arm assigned at random, the slope on attained capability is the elasticity plus a term that has the sign of the product of the latent factor’s effects on capability and on service and vanishes with it, the arm contrast at matched capability is the arm’s direct effect less the arm’s effect on capability times that term, and the total effect is the direct effect plus the arm’s effect on capability times the elasticity. So χol\chi_{ol}, its contrasts and GembG_{\mathrm{emb}} read at matched CC are identified where capability is varied by assignment (administered capability, or target difficulty crossed with the arms) or under a no-confounding premise stated before any outcome, and not by crossed or off-path variation in attained capability alone (registration version 1.102, line 621), which is necessary and not sufficient; the report says whether the model’s ln⁡(C/C0)\ln(C/C_0) is assigned or attained. Curved and broken-regime rivals, a two-part or censored model for zero service, and a flexible comparator form the closed model set; the power law must win prospectively; no selection rule is chosen here.

6.5 The registered faces, whole

P21. Its refuter, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1227):

REFUTED BY: no interaction between correction placement and depth beyond the tolerance registered with that instrument, in a design whose own sensitivity shows an interaction of that size would have been detected. A design too small to find the interaction is a failed instrument and not a refutation, as condition D already provides.

A constant advantage is scored against it (registration version 1.102, line 1229): “an embedded arm that beats the external arm by the same margin at every depth is reported as a level difference and is scored against this proposition, not for it”. A supported result establishes an access interaction, not physical or architectural embedding (registration version 1.102, line 1223), and not an exponent (registration version 1.102, line 1221); it does not resolve the trade-off the registration states (registration version 1.102, line 1235), quoted in Section 6.7. The registration’s text gives P21’s instrument as a design draft (registration version 1.102, line 1243: “INSTRUMENT: DESIGN DRAFT, the embedded-versus-external correction designs. That unit’s registered sensitivity was measured on a smaller design than the one registered, and its negative-slope hypothesis has no operating characteristic; both are recorded against that unit and are closed before this proposition is scored.”); Section 11 states where P21’s counted test stands. A widening advantage arriving without the registered fall in the monitor’s detection rate is reported as unexplained (registration version 1.102, line 1233). What falls with it, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1237): “FALLS WITH IT: the protocol’s engineering case, jointly with P12, P13 and P15. The three laws are untouched, which is why it is registered separately from them.”

On the counted instrument that has decided P21, Unit 83, the counted test of in-loop correction with depth (Section 11), depth is the count of administered arrivals, drawn from a sealed bank and none revised twice (registration version 1.105, P21, the deciding instrument on the counted route), so no uncorrected fault can seed a later one, and the route by which recursion as such widens the in-round advantage (Section 6.8) is absent by design; with the in-round detection rate and the arrivals’ fault rate unchanged by depth, a widening there comes from how the outside arm’s detection, or its rejection of sound work, changes with the size of what it sees (Proposition V-4(e)).

One limit of the frozen design bears on that reading. The monitor was told to accept the entries “only if every entry shown meets the charter for its case”, and it was shown every entry it had already accepted together with the arriving one. A rejection removed nothing already accepted, and its score counted only the arriving entry: one for a sound entry accepted, minus one for a faulty entry accepted, nothing for a rejection. So once it had accepted a faulty entry, a monitor that followed its instruction would reject every later entry, sound ones included, and each sound entry rejected scored nothing. That widens the lead with depth without any fall in what the monitor detects: in the terms of Proposition V-4, with yk=0y_{\mathrm{k}} = 0, the outside arm’s rejection of sound work rises as depth grows. Unit 83b’s registration records a descriptive split of that run’s widening of 0.0100 a round: 0.0024 from a fall in the monitor’s catch rate, 0.0035 from rising false alarms and 0.0041 from earlier misses, the part that arises after an accepted faulty entry (graded there as moderate confidence). Nothing in that run is re-scored, because its registration and code are frozen. Unit 83b, its registered successor on three providers, keeps the same prompts and scoring; before its first call a dated addendum on its registration will name this limit and read its share on that study’s mechanism axis.

P12. Its refuter, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1035):

REFUTED BY: a preregistered manipulation of build order producing no change in the correction-leverage exponent beyond the tolerance registered with that instrument, where the instrument has shown from its own sensitivity that a change of that size would have been detected. A manipulation too weak to move anything is not a refutation of this prediction; it is a failed instrument, and condition D above says so in advance.

Its endpoint is the exponent on one scale, scored as a continuous claim (registration version 1.102, line 1039: “It is a continuous claim and it is scored as one.”); the minimum effect is 0.10, and “A future instrument may register a smaller minimum and may not register a larger one” (registration version 1.102, line 1041); its instrument line reads NONE, “one endpoint away from an instrument” (registration version 1.102, line 1045); what would decide it is a typed extension of the correction-exponent estimator across the maximal contrast with a joint interval (registration version 1.102, line 1049). Support is read on that joint interval: an interval establishing a change of at least the minimum effect, in either direction, supports P12; a change smaller than the minimum “is reported as no effect of interest rather than as no effect” (registration version 1.102, line 1041), whatever its significance; an upward change so established supports P12 and supports the build-order limb, a downward change so established supports P12 and refutes the limb (Section 6.6, item 2; registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the build-order limb), and both verdicts are reported. A supported result “does not license any statement about where the boundary sits, about a system built in that order being safer, or about orders outside that contrast” (registration version 1.102, line 1047). What falls with it, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 1043): “FALLS WITH IT: the programme’s argument that build order is an intervention point rather than an accident of history, and this proposition’s share of the protocol’s engineering case, which it carries jointly with P13, P15 and P21.”

6.6 Kill condition K-V

Stated before any data, consistent with P12 (no direction) and P21 as registered. Version 1.103 fixed the ARC Embedding Law’s kill condition and verdict rule: Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is refuted by a refuted build-order limb, by a refuted P21 (by its registered refuter, by a constant advantage scored against it, or by an interval its directional reading scores against it), or by a refuted verdict on the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb through the registered dependence, and by no other result; it is SUPPORTED only when both limbs are supported and no refuted verdict on Law IV’s comparison limb strikes it; an undecided limb never refutes it; and in every other case it is UNDER TEST, with each limb’s verdict printed beside the law’s word and the verdict on P21’s mechanism axis beside the placement limb’s (registration version 1.105, Law V, its kill condition, its verdict rule and its dependence on ARC-4). From version 1.105 that refuted verdict is a refuted P23, and an inconclusive, untested or NOT EVALUABLE P23 strikes nothing (registration version 1.105, the dependence’s entry). The items below state each limb’s rule in this document’s terms; where a clause of an earlier version went beyond the registered refuters, it is marked, and version 1.103’s rule stands in its place. None changes P12’s or P21’s scoring.

  1. Placement limb. Struck when P21’s registered refuter fires: in the registered design (registration version 1.102, line 1231), passing its sensitivity and validity gates, no interaction between placement and depth beyond the registered tolerance. Struck equally by a constant advantage established within the registered tolerance by a design meeting the sensitivity clause, which is P21’s refuter itself (registration version 1.102, lines 1227 and 1229). Struck also by an interval P21’s directional reading scores against it: an interval for the interaction lying wholly below the positive tolerance, in a design whose own sensitivity shows that an interaction of the tolerance’s size would have been detected, or an interval lying wholly below the negative tolerance, which shows a narrowing (registration version 1.105, P21, the directional reading). Version 1.1 of this document set out, as a law-level convention, a strike on an interval lying wholly on the side in which the external arm’s advantage widens; the registered reading takes its place. A P21 refutation strikes the limb by these rules; it does not measure the mechanism reading and does not prove ηo,in≤ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} \le \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}}. A failed instrument is NOT EVALUABLE, never survival, and never a refutation.

  2. Build-order limb. Struck when P12’s registered refuter fires: a preregistered manipulation on the registered maximal contrast producing no change in the correction-leverage exponent beyond the registered tolerance (0.10 on the exponent scale, or the smaller minimum a future instrument registers), with demonstrated sensitivity. On the joint interval that is an interval lying inside the tolerance band from −0.10-0.10 to +0.10+0.10, open at its ends, since a change of exactly the minimum is a change “by at least the registered minimum effect” (registration version 1.102, line 1033); an interval whose end falls inside the at-the-margin band the instrument fixed around the tolerance is a result at the margin, not a verdict (registration version 1.102, line 391). An interval establishing a change of at least the minimum in either direction supports P12 and the limb’s registered face. The limb’s directed claim, the genesis reading of Section 6.1, equation (9), is struck by one rule, which this document stated in advance and version 1.103 registers as the limb’s (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the build-order limb): an interval on χfirst−χafter\chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}}, at the placement the instrument fixes and on the scale Condition B fixes (registration version 1.102, line 403; Section 7.7), whose upper end lies below the registered minimum, 0.10, or below the smaller minimum a future instrument registers. The rule is the exact interval complement of the reading: the reading is false at every point of an interval exactly when the interval’s upper end lies below the minimum, and it holds at every point exactly when the lower end is at or above it. The rule that strikes on an interval lying wholly on the adverse side (its upper end below zero) is a special case of this rule, since an upper end below zero lies below the minimum; and the rule strikes the reading wherever P12’s registered refuter fires, since an interval inside the open band has its upper end below the minimum, as the reading’s implying P12 requires. An interval whose upper end falls inside the at-the-margin band around the minimum is a result at the margin for the reading as it is for P12 (registration version 1.102, line 391). The rule needs no separate sensitivity clause, because an interval lying wholly below the minimum itself excludes an effect of the registered size in the claimed direction, but a failed instrument or a missing identification of the construct is not cured by a narrow interval. It strikes the limb and changes nothing in P12’s mark. Wherever a term of P12’s exponent is judged by a person or by a model, the scoring gate holds the limb’s reading at untested until that gate passes (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the build-order limb). The worked cases, each read with its ends clear of the at-the-margin bands the instrument fixes: an interval from −0.30-0.30 to +0.05+0.05 is INCONCLUSIVE under P12’s registered refuter, whatever the sensitivity, because it is not inside the tolerance band and so does not show “no change in the correction-leverage exponent beyond the tolerance registered with that instrument”, and it does not support P12, because it does not establish a change of at least the minimum; it strikes the limb’s reading, since its upper end 0.05 lies below 0.10. An interval from +0.02+0.02 to +0.08+0.08, on which formation first carries the higher elasticity at every point but by less than the minimum at every point, strikes the reading as well, and with its sensitivity shown it fires P12’s registered refuter too, so the reading and P12 fall together there. P12 is read in neither direction by any of this. Registration version 1.104 states this limb’s refutation in two places, and they differ: the paragraph on the build-order limb refutes it on every interval lying wholly below the minimum effect, and the successor qualification inside P12’s entry refutes it only on an interval lying wholly at or beyond the minimum effect on the side of the corrector added after, or where P12’s own refuter fires (registration version 1.104, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, the build-order limb, and P12, its successor qualification). They give different verdicts on intervals such as −0.30-0.30 to +0.05+0.05, and on intervals inside the band from a design whose sensitivity is not shown. This report follows the paragraph on the limb, and version 1.105 resolves the difference the same way: the rule of the paragraph on the limb, the stricter, is the one rule by which the limb is refuted, and the qualification inside P12’s entry is read by it (registration version 1.105, the qualification that one rule refutes the build-order limb; Section 10, item 15).

  3. Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, as a whole (fixed by version 1.103). Three ways of reading the two limbs as one law were on the record in earlier versions of this document: severable limbs, under which the whole law is refuted only when both limbs are struck, which was version 0.2.1’s default; a strict conjunction, under which either strike refutes it; and a law that stands on the placement limb alone. Version 1.103 fixed the reading before any data, in the verdict rule stated at the head of this section (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, its verdict rule). Each limb is scored by its own rule, items 1 and 2, and a struck limb is reported as struck. A refuted P15 alone refutes Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, and leaves Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, to its own limbs (Section 8, item 3). The mechanism reading is scored apart from both limbs, and the genesis reading is now the build-order limb’s own claim (item 2). The boundary reading falls with the ARC Ceiling’s model, which takes nothing from either limb.

  4. What is not a refutation of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law (in the registration’s own terms, registration version 1.102, line 121): a failed instrument; a P20 estimate of the direct depth-dependence, which is scored in ARC-3 alone and may not cross scopes (registration version 1.102, line 247); an offsetting elasticity invented after a null; a level difference offered as an interaction; and any result on composition class or failure-mode independence, which P21’s unit does not vary (registration version 1.102, line 1223). Version 1.103 registers the same list for Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, and adds a refuted P15 alone (registration version 1.105, Law V, its kill condition).

  5. The weaker neighbour. What survives the ARC Embedding Law’s refutation: the identities of Section 6.3, the verdicts on P12 and P21 as engineering results under their own numbers, and Laws I to III untouched (registration version 1.102, line 1237); what falls is what registration version 1.102, lines 1043 and 1237 name, quoted in Section 6.5; version 1.103 registers the same (registration version 1.105, Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, what a refuted Law V leaves standing).

6.7 What the embedding mathematics does not say

It does not say that embedded correction is safe, sufficient or superior on any axis but the one P21 scores. Nor does it say that embedding a model of harm makes its use for avoidance hard to invert: such a model is dual-use, and a small readout of it, a final projection or its sign, may be a cheap direction to change, since Proposition IV-U’s least capability cost of lowering a property is zero along flat directions, of which a small readout is a candidate. A supported P21 does not resolve the trade-off the registration states (registration version 1.102, line 1235): “embedding correction in the substrate that computes maximises the corrector’s scaling with capability and minimises its independence from the generator, because a corrector built into the system shares the system’s blind spots by construction. Those are the two axes named in the admissibility conditions above, and embedding moves them in opposite directions. Whether the gain on scaling outweighs the loss on independence is not registered here and is not decided by this proposition.” A supported P12 licenses nothing about safety (registration version 1.102, line 1047). The identities of Section 6.3 identify no partial from one path, and the mechanism reading of registration version 1.102, line 1239 is measured by no verdict here. Nothing in this section has been measured.

6.8 Two minimal models for Law V, the ARC Embedding Law (the report’s own models; not registered)

Sections 6.1 to 6.7 give Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, definitions, identities, an estimation design and the logic of its verdicts; they derive neither limb. This section states, for each limb, the smallest model in which it can be derived or can fail. Each model says what a test must measure, and neither is evidence for the law.

The placement model.

Revision runs in rounds 1,…,R1, \dots, R, and depth is the round count. In the propagation setting, fresh faults arrive at mean rate q>0q > 0 a round, and each uncorrected fault present seeds on average σ≥0\sigma \ge 0 new faults in the next round, so that an uncorrected error feeds later work. The in-round arm removes each new fault in its own round with probability δin\delta_{\mathrm{in}}; the outside arm corrects nothing during the rounds and removes each fault of the finished output with probability δout\delta_{\mathrm{out}}, which may depend on the output’s size and so on RR. For σ>0\sigma > 0 the expected faults left are Nin(R)=q(1+σ(1−δin))R−1σ,Nout(R)=(1−δout)q(1+σ)R−1σ,\begin{equation*} N_{\mathrm{in}}(R) = q\,\frac{(1 + \sigma(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{in}}))^R - 1}{\sigma}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{out}}(R) = (1 - \delta_{\mathrm{out}})\,q\,\frac{(1 + \sigma)^R - 1}{\sigma}, \end{equation*}(14) and q(1−δin)Rq(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{in}})R and q(1−δout)Rq(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{out}})R at σ=0\sigma = 0; the advantage is adv(R):=Nout(R)−Nin(R)\mathrm{adv}(R) := N_{\mathrm{out}}(R) - N_{\mathrm{in}}(R). In the arrivals setting, one unit of work arrives in each arm each round, faulty with probability qq, independently of everything before: arrivals from a fixed bank, none revised twice, so σ=0\sigma = 0 by construction. The in-round arm detects a faulty arrival with probability δin\delta_{\mathrm{in}} and repairs it; the outside arm sees only the register and can only keep an arrival out, which it does to a faulty arrival with probability δout\delta_{\mathrm{out}} and to a sound one with probability δoutfalse\delta^{\mathrm{false}}_{\mathrm{out}}, two rates that may change with depth. A committed sound unit scores +1+1, a committed faulty unit −1-1 and an entry kept out yky_{\mathrm{k}}, with −1≤yk≤1-1 \le y_{\mathrm{k}} \le 1: an entry kept out scores no better than a committed sound unit and no worse than a committed faulty one; lead(R)\mathrm{lead}(R) is the in-round arm’s mean score in round RR less the outside arm’s, and keptin(R)\mathrm{kept}_{\mathrm{in}}(R) and keptout(R)\mathrm{kept}_{\mathrm{out}}(R) are the two arms’ rates of keeping entries out.

Proposition V-4 (the placement model; the report’s own models, not registered). In the placement model:

  1. With no seeding, σ=0\sigma = 0, and a constant δout\delta_{\mathrm{out}}, the advantage is adv(R)=qR(δin−δout)\mathrm{adv}(R) = qR(\delta_{\mathrm{in}} - \delta_{\mathrm{out}}): the same advantage in every round, a level, which a cumulative endpoint shows as a widening.

  2. With σ>0\sigma > 0, 0<δin<10 < \delta_{\mathrm{in}} < 1 and δout\delta_{\mathrm{out}} constant below one, the ratio Nout(R)/Nin(R)N_{\mathrm{out}}(R)/N_{\mathrm{in}}(R) rises at every depth and grows without bound, like (1−δout)[(1+σ)/(1+σ(1−δin))]R(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{out}})[(1 + \sigma)/(1 + \sigma(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{in}}))]^R, so the in-round arm pulls away even from an outside arm that removes each fault more reliably. With equal detection, δin=δout=δ\delta_{\mathrm{in}} = \delta_{\mathrm{out}} = \delta with 0<δ<10 < \delta < 1, the advantage is zero at depth one and rises at every later depth: its increment from depth R−1R - 1 to RR is q(1−δ)[(1+σ)R−1−(1+σ(1−δ))R−1]q(1 - \delta)[(1 + \sigma)^{R-1} - (1 + \sigma(1 - \delta))^{R-1}], positive for R≥2R \ge 2.

  3. With σ>0\sigma > 0 and 0<δin<δout<10 < \delta_{\mathrm{in}} < \delta_{\mathrm{out}} < 1, both constant, the widening is of the ratio, or of the logarithm of the ratio, from depth one, and of the difference adv(R)\mathrm{adv}(R) only beyond the turning depth Rturn=1+ln⁡[(1−δin)/(1−δout)]ln⁡[(1+σ)/(1+σ(1−δin))];\begin{equation*} R_{\mathrm{turn}} = 1 + \frac{\ln[(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{in}})/(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{out}})]}{\ln[(1 + \sigma)/(1 + \sigma(1 - \delta_{\mathrm{in}}))]}; \end{equation*}(15) the difference falls at every depth below RturnR_{\mathrm{turn}} and rises at every depth above it. At δin=0\delta_{\mathrm{in}} = 0 the two growth factors are equal: the ratio is the constant 1−δout1 - \delta_{\mathrm{out}}, there is no turning depth, and the difference falls at every depth.

  4. In the arrivals setting, lead=2qδin+(1−q)(1−yk)δoutfalse−q(1+yk)δout\mathrm{lead} = 2q\delta_{\mathrm{in}} + (1 - q)(1 - y_{\mathrm{k}})\,\delta^{\mathrm{false}}_{\mathrm{out}} - q(1 + y_{\mathrm{k}})\,\delta_{\mathrm{out}}. With the outside rates constant in depth, the lead is constant, whatever the two arms’ actions; with equal detection δ\delta and no false rejection it is qδ(1−yk)q\delta(1 - y_{\mathrm{k}}), the value of repairing an entry rather than keeping it out.

  5. With the in-round detection rate and the arrivals’ fault rate constant in depth, the slope of the lead in depth is (1−q)(1−yk)dδoutfalse/dR−q(1+yk)dδout/dR(1 - q)(1 - y_{\mathrm{k}})\,\mathrm{d}\delta^{\mathrm{false}}_{\mathrm{out}}/\mathrm{d}R - q(1 + y_{\mathrm{k}})\,\mathrm{d}\delta_{\mathrm{out}}/\mathrm{d}R, so, both coefficients being non-negative over the range of yky_{\mathrm{k}}, the lead widens only if the outside arm’s rejection of sound work rises with depth or its detection of faulty work falls. Where the in-round detection rate moves with depth the slope gains 2qdδin/dR2q\,\mathrm{d}\delta_{\mathrm{in}}/\mathrm{d}R, and where the fault rate moves it gains (dq/dR)[2δin−(1−yk)δoutfalse−(1+yk)δout](\mathrm{d}q/\mathrm{d}R)[2\delta_{\mathrm{in}} - (1 - y_{\mathrm{k}})\delta^{\mathrm{false}}_{\mathrm{out}} - (1 + y_{\mathrm{k}})\delta_{\mathrm{out}}].

  6. For any estimate of the lead’s slope that is linear in the entries’ scores, such as the least-squares slope of the per-round means, the slope at score yky_{\mathrm{k}} is the slope at score zero less yky_{\mathrm{k}} times the estimated slope of keptout−keptin\mathrm{kept}_{\mathrm{out}} - \mathrm{kept}_{\mathrm{in}}. This needs nothing beyond that linearity.

(Proof: Appendix A.13.)

So the placement limb follows in the model from either of two premises and fails without them: an uncorrected fault seeds later faults (σ>0\sigma > 0), or the outside arm’s detection falls, or its rejection of sound work rises, as what it inspects grows. With independent arrivals, outside rates that do not change with depth, and an in-round detection rate and a fault rate that do not change with it either, the advantage is a constant level, which P21 scores against; a design that reads the mechanism therefore prints the in-round arm’s detection by depth beside the outside arm’s two rates. Part (a) says that only a per-round endpoint tells a widening from an accumulated level; P21’s counted endpoint is per round (Section 6.5). Part (c) says that the scale of the endpoint can decide its sign: with σ=0.3\sigma = 0.3, δin=0.5\delta_{\mathrm{in}} = 0.5, δout=0.8\delta_{\mathrm{out}} = 0.8 and q=1q = 1, adv(R)\mathrm{adv}(R) falls from −0.30-0.30 at depth one to −2.09-2.09 at depth eight, rises from depth nine and is first positive, +0.36+0.36, at depth twelve, with Rturn=8.47R_{\mathrm{turn}} = 8.47, while the ratio rises at every depth. A difference endpoint read below RturnR_{\mathrm{turn}} gives the interaction the wrong sign, so a design that means to test recursion as such fixes its endpoint’s scale and its depth range with RturnR_{\mathrm{turn}} in view. Part (f) is a data identity, and it bears on any counted design that scores an entry kept out. On the counted instrument that has decided P21, σ=0\sigma = 0 by construction (Section 6.5).

The build-order model.

A ladder of targets is indexed by capability C≥C0C \ge C_0, each formed by capability training from C0C_0. A corrector’s service on a target is Q=mis(C)cvgQ = \mathrm{mis}(C)\,\mathrm{cvg}, with mis(C)\mathrm{mis}(C) the misalignment present and cvg∈[0,1]\mathrm{cvg} \in [0, 1] the corrector’s coverage of the target’s faults; the misalignment present is taken to be the same under both orders at one target, so that it cancels in the contrast (the cancellation premise). Two correctors carry the same content, nex>0n_{\mathrm{ex}} > 0 examples. The corrector added after is formed against the finished target, and by the learning premise its coverage falls as the target’s representation grows: cvgafter(C)=nex/(nex+rep(C))\mathrm{cvg}_{\mathrm{after}}(C) = n_{\mathrm{ex}}/(n_{\mathrm{ex}} + \mathrm{rep}(C)) with rep(C)=rep(C0)(C/C0)erep\mathrm{rep}(C) = \mathrm{rep}(C_0)\,(C/C_0)^{e_{\mathrm{rep}}} and erep≥0e_{\mathrm{rep}} \ge 0, the shape of a linear read-out learned from nexn_{\mathrm{ex}} examples in a representation of size rep\mathrm{rep}. The corrector formed first is formed at C0C_0 with the same content, so the two coverages agree there, and is carried through the formation of capability after it. By the decay premise its coverage is multiplied by a retention factor ret(C)\mathrm{ret}(C), with ret(C0)=1\mathrm{ret}(C_0) = 1 and decay elasticity hfirst:=−dln⁡ret/dln⁡C≥0h_{\mathrm{first}} := -\mathrm{d}\ln\mathrm{ret}/\mathrm{d}\ln C \ge 0, which the erosion of its own installed function under later capability training (the object of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, where the corrector is part of the target) or the drift of the target’s faults away from what it learned (where it is separate) can make positive. By the co-scaling premise, where it reads the target’s own improving representation, its coverage also gains a factor (C/C0)eco(C/C_0)^{e_{\mathrm{co}}} with eco≥0e_{\mathrm{co}} \ge 0; the premise holds only on the range of capability on which that coverage stays at most one, which with constant elasticities and eco>hfirste_{\mathrm{co}} > h_{\mathrm{first}} is C/C0≤[(nex+rep(C0))/nex]1/(eco−hfirst)C/C_0 \le [(n_{\mathrm{ex}} + \mathrm{rep}(C_0))/n_{\mathrm{ex}}]^{1/(e_{\mathrm{co}} - h_{\mathrm{first}})}. The exponents are χfirst\chi_{\mathrm{first}} and χafter\chi_{\mathrm{after}}, the capability elasticities of the two correctors’ service.

Proposition V-5 (the build-order model; the report’s own models, not registered). In the build-order model:

  1. Locally, χfirst−χafter=eco−hfirst+ereprep(C)nex+rep(C);\begin{equation*} \chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}} = e_{\mathrm{co}} - h_{\mathrm{first}} + e_{\mathrm{rep}}\,\frac{\mathrm{rep}(C)}{n_{\mathrm{ex}} + \mathrm{rep}(C)}; \end{equation*}(16) with constant elasticities, the estimate of the contrast across two rungs C1<C2C_1 < C_2 lies in the closed interval from eco−hfirste_{\mathrm{co}} - h_{\mathrm{first}} to eco−hfirst+erepe_{\mathrm{co}} - h_{\mathrm{first}} + e_{\mathrm{rep}}.

  2. Where hfirst≤ecoh_{\mathrm{first}} \le e_{\mathrm{co}} the contrast is non-negative, and it reaches P12’s registered minimum effect where the right side of equation (16) is at least 0.10.

  3. Where hfirst≥eco+ereph_{\mathrm{first}} \ge e_{\mathrm{co}} + e_{\mathrm{rep}}, the contrast and every two-rung estimate of it are at most zero, and negative where hfirst>ecoh_{\mathrm{first}} > e_{\mathrm{co}}: the corrector formed first has the smaller exponent, the reverse of the limb.

  4. Where log-capability rises at the rate dln⁡C/dτ\mathrm{d}\ln C/\mathrm{d}\tau in the time τ\tau of later training and the formed-first corrector keeps the fraction S(τ)S(\tau) of its installed function, ret(C)=S(τ(C))\mathrm{ret}(C) = S(\tau(C)), the decay elasticity is hfirst=h(τ)/(dln⁡C/dτ)h_{\mathrm{first}} = h(\tau)/(\mathrm{d}\ln C/\mathrm{d}\tau), with h(τ):=−dln⁡S/dτh(\tau) := -\mathrm{d}\ln S/\mathrm{d}\tau the log-decay rate of Section 5.6 written in time rather than budget.

  5. Under Assumption S, an early corrector installed with the capability loss in its objective decays no faster than one installed externally, by the ratio statement of Theorem IV-C, so with the other premises the same its build-order contrast is at least as large.

  6. A refuted comparison limb of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, leaves the sign of the contrast open, since the contrast depends on the level of decay and not on the comparison; and a supported build-order limb says nothing about that comparison limb.

(Proof: Appendix A.14.)

So build order alone does not decide the sign of the build-order contrast: it is the late corrector’s learning penalty, plus any co-scaling, less the decay of the early corrector’s coverage as capability is formed after it (Section 6.1 states the consequence for the limb). Parts (d) and (e) tie the size of that decay to the persistence Section 5.9 models. Part (f) agrees with the registration, which fixes the ARC Embedding Law’s dependence on the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb as “A REGISTERED DEPENDENCE FIXED IN ADVANCE AND NOT AN ENTAILMENT” (registration version 1.105, Law V’s dependence on ARC-4). The cancellation premise is a premise and not a finding: where the early corrector acts while the capability is being formed, the misalignment present at the target is itself an outcome of the order, and the contrast then mixes coverage with load. An instrument for P12 that measures each corrector’s coverage on a standard injected load keeps the contrast the model’s.

Standing.

Both models were stated, and read a second time within the programme, on 17 November 2026; that is not an independent check. A search of 17 November 2026, twenty-two queries in two families, half of them for the opposite (on OpenAlex and the web, since arXiv’s query interface refused automated requests that day), with twelve works read at their official records, each at its abstract, found earlier statements bearing on the premises of both models, for and against them (Section 2), and found neither model’s results stated in what was read.

7 The balance identity and Law III, the ARC Ceiling, unchanged

7.1 Identity B-1 (the local balance identity)

Let QQ and WW be positive differentiable correction service and newly generated burden on one clock, in comparable units with any conversion fixed before outcomes, on the same domain as Section 6.2. Along a specified path C(R)C(R), with other factors fixed, Δbal:=dln⁡(Q/W)/dln⁡R=αR(χ−κ)+(η−ζ).\begin{equation*} \Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} := \mathrm{d}\ln(Q/W)/\mathrm{d}\ln R = \alpha_R(\chi - \kappa) + (\eta - \zeta). \end{equation*}(17)

Proof: subtract the chain rules for ln⁡Q\ln Q and ln⁡W\ln W along the path. Every elasticity is local; no power law is assumed. Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} is the programme’s balance exponent read locally, and the registration’s Δbalance=ϕQ−ϕW\Delta_{\mathrm{balance}} = \phi_Q - \phi_W (Eastwood 2026j; registration version 1.102, line 619: “the balance exponent is Delta_balance = phi_Q - phi_W: correction service minus burden”); positive means correction is gaining on burden. The registration’s elasticities are log-derivatives “with respect to the resource clock” (registration version 1.102, line 619); Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} above is per unit of ln⁡R\ln R, so the two agree where the clock is depth, and otherwise differ by the factor dln⁡R\mathrm{d}\ln R divided by dln\mathrm{d}\ln of the clock. That factor is positive, and so preserves the sign and the zero set, wherever depth rises with the clock at a positive rate; along a stretch on which depth fell as the clock advanced it would be negative and would reverse the sign. The clock condition is the author’s: the service clock need not equal the resource coordinate, but it must be fixed within a model, and changing it changes the operational quantities.

7.2 Proposition B-2 (the balance root and the sign rule)

Proposition B-2. Where κ\kappa differs from χ\chi, Δbal=0\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} = 0 has the single root αR=αbal:=(η−ζ)/(κ−χ),\begin{equation*} \alpha_R = \alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} := (\eta - \zeta)/(\kappa - \chi), \end{equation*}(18) and identically Δbal=(κ−χ)(αbal−αR).\begin{equation*} \Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} = (\kappa - \chi)(\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} - \alpha_R). \end{equation*}(19) Hence: with κ>χ\kappa > \chi the trend is favourable exactly where αR<αbal\alpha_R < \alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}, and αbal\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} is a ceiling, written αcrit\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}; with κ<χ\kappa < \chi the inequality reverses and αbal\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} is a floor; with κ=χ\kappa = \chi the trend is η−ζ\eta - \zeta, independent of αR\alpha_R.

The symbol αcrit\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} is used only in the ceiling case, so that the entry of the programme’s notation (Eastwood 2026g), the stability ceiling, keeps its meaning; its range there, at least one, holds exactly where η−ζ≥κ−χ>0\eta - \zeta \ge \kappa - \chi > 0, which in the registered burden model (κ=1\kappa = 1, ζ=−1\zeta = -1) is η≥−χ\eta \ge -\chi with χ<1\chi < 1: in the pacing case η=−1/2\eta = -1/2 with χ=0\chi = 0 gives a ceiling of one half; outside it, κ=1/2\kappa = 1/2 with χ=1\chi = 1, η=0\eta = 0 and ζ=−1\zeta = -1 gives αbal=−2\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} = -2, a floor. A non-positive αcrit\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} with κ>χ\kappa > \chi leaves no positive growth elasticity with a favourable trend. As χ\chi rises to κ\kappa with η−ζ>0\eta - \zeta > 0 the boundary grows without bound: a correction elasticity matching the total burden elasticity leaves no finite boundary. The zero set of Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}}, the balance frontier, is this set of points; it depends on the path field αR\alpha_R as well as on the service and burden surfaces. Once the path field is specified, Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} is a function on the (C,R)(C, R) plane and its zero set is a level set of that function: where Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} is continuously differentiable, the set is a curve near each of its points at which the gradient of Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} does not vanish (the implicit function theorem), so it is generically a curve, but not always: in the pacing case at χ=1\chi = 1 with η=−1\eta = -1, Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} is zero everywhere, and at χ=1/2\chi = 1/2 and η=0\eta = 0 with the field αR=1\alpha_R = 1 it is one half everywhere, so the set is then the whole plane or empty. Before the field is specified the set lies in (C,R,αR)(C, R, \alpha_R), where the derivative of Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} in αR\alpha_R is χ−κ\chi - \kappa, so, again where the elasticities are continuously differentiable, it is a surface near each of its points at which κ\kappa differs from χ\chi; it carries no symbol here and Law III, the ARC Ceiling, is unchanged (Section 9).

7.3 Corollary B-3 (the registered special case)

Corollary B-3. Under the registered premises, burden proportional to dC/dR\mathrm{d}C/\mathrm{d}R along a power-law path, read as the programme’s notation reads the registered model, the surface WW proportional to αC/R\alpha C/R with κ=1\kappa = 1 and ζ=−1\zeta = -1 (one path alone does not fix the partials, Section 6.3), and correction proportional to CχC^{\chi} (η=0\eta = 0), αcrit=1/(1−χ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1 - \chi): the frozen Law III, the ARC Ceiling, verbatim (registration version 1.102, line 665): “Law III, the ARC Ceiling, alpha_crit = 1 / (1 - gamma): the growth exponent is capped by the reciprocal of the correction shortfall.”

The registration’s letter, the one inside that quotation, and this document’s χ\chi name the same quantity (registration version 1.102, line 305). The mapping is a symbol mapping inside the stated pacing model and is not permission to identify the ARC Co-Scaling Law’s βC\beta_C with either: “WHETHER THE SECOND LAW’S EXPONENT AND THE THIRD LAW’S ARE ONE QUANTITY IS NOT SETTLED HERE AND IS RECORDED AS UNESTABLISHED BELOW, and no proposition assumes they are.” (registration version 1.102, line 271). Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, is “beta_C exceeds k” (registration version 1.102, line 663). Paper X (Eastwood 2026b) defines kk by fractional growth, (dC/dt)/C=bCk(\mathrm{d}C/\mathrm{d}t)/C = bC^k. On the depth clock, along a power-law path C∝RαC \propto R^{\alpha}, the fractional growth is (dC/dR)/C=α/R(\mathrm{d}C/\mathrm{d}R)/C = \alpha/R, which is proportional to C−1/αC^{-1/\alpha}, so k=−1/αk = -1/\alpha, and the relative criterion βC>k\beta_C > k, under which the misalignment fraction vanishes, holds wherever βC>−1/α\beta_C > -1/\alpha and does not give the ceiling. The reciprocal form comes from Paper X’s absolute criterion, its Corollary 1: absolute misalignment stays bounded where βC≥k+1\beta_C \ge k + 1 and tends to zero where βC>k+1\beta_C > k + 1. On the depth clock these read βC≥1−1/α\beta_C \ge 1 - 1/\alpha and βC>1−1/α\beta_C > 1 - 1/\alpha, that is α≤1/(1−βC)\alpha \le 1/(1 - \beta_C) and α<1/(1−βC)\alpha < 1/(1 - \beta_C) for α>0\alpha > 0 and βC<1\beta_C < 1. The registration’s drift exponent, the exponent of the burden itself, is (α−1)/α(\alpha - 1)/\alpha under the burden model (registration version 1.102, line 637), which is this kk plus one, so the criterion read against it is the absolute one. A change of clock, with depth advancing in time at a rate proportional to CδC^{\delta}, adds δ\delta to both exponents and leaves their difference unchanged, so each criterion reads the same on either clock: on that wall clock k=δ−1/αk = \delta - 1/\alpha, which equals (α−1)/α(\alpha - 1)/\alpha only where δ=1\delta = 1, a cycle time proportional to 1/C1/C. The absolute criterion returns the ceiling relation only under the identification βC=χ\beta_C = \chi, which the registration records as unestablished (registration version 1.102, lines 271, 309 and 613) and which needs an intervention designed to move one while leaving the other before either stands in for the other (registration version 1.102, line 1029). Under that identification, and only under it, “The ceiling is the co-scaling criterion with the drift exponent fixed by the burden model.” (registration version 1.102, line 637), and Law III, the ARC Ceiling, remains a conditional quantitative consequence of Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, under its stated identifications, not an independent finding. Laws II and III, the ARC Co-Scaling Law and the ARC Ceiling, are each a law under test.

7.4 The pacing family

In the pacing case (κ=1\kappa = 1, ζ=−1\zeta = -1) with a direct depth term, αcrit=(1+η)/(1−χ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = (1 + \eta)/(1 - \chi), a positive ceiling for χ<1\chi < 1 and 1+η>01 + \eta > 0; at χ=1\chi = 1 the trend is 1+η1 + \eta independent of αR\alpha_R; at χ>1\chi > 1 with 1+η≥01 + \eta \ge 0 the trend αR(χ−1)+(1+η)\alpha_R(\chi - 1) + (1 + \eta) is positive for every positive αR\alpha_R, as the sum of a positive and a non-negative term. At χ=1/2\chi = 1/2 this family gives 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta). That value is not the general boundary: 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta) is the pacing-case value; the general boundary at χ=1/2\chi = 1/2 is (η−ζ)/(κ−1/2)(\eta - \zeta)/(\kappa - 1/2), which equals 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta) for every η\eta only when κ=1\kappa = 1 and ζ=−1\zeta = -1; at single points the two can agree elsewhere (κ=3/2\kappa = 3/2, ζ=−2\zeta = -2 and η=0\eta = 0 give two on both sides), a coincidence at one point that does not make 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta) the general boundary. So, in the pacing special case, at the same-class cap χ=1/2\chi = 1/2, the boundary is 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta), and the ARC Bound, α≤2\alpha \le 2 on the relative rung, is its η=0\eta = 0 value.

The registration’s four-quantity form (registration version 1.102, line 639: “the boundary is one plus the difference of the two direct depth-dependences, divided by one plus the burden intensity less the correction elasticity”) is the same boundary written with the registered model’s values subtracted: the burden intensity of that sentence is κ−1\kappa - 1 (the programme’s μB\mu_B) and its direct depth-dependence of burden is ζ+1\zeta + 1, not ζ\zeta, whose name in the programme’s notation, the direct depth-dependence of burden, is the full depth elasticity of WW at fixed CC; so (1+η−(ζ+1))/(1+(κ−1)−χ)(1 + \eta - (\zeta + 1))/(1 + (\kappa - 1) - \chi) is (η−ζ)/(κ−χ)(\eta - \zeta)/(\kappa - \chi) identically, and the registration’s “both direct terms and the burden intensity vanish” is ζ+1=0\zeta + 1 = 0 and κ−1=0\kappa - 1 = 0 with η=0\eta = 0. Its worked numbers hold: χ=1/2\chi = 1/2 with η=1/2\eta = 1/2 gives three; χ=4/5\chi = 4/5 gives five; both together give seven and a half. Two is the relative rung’s value: it bounds whether the ratio of correction service to burden improves. A stricter question asks whether the absolute burden a system carries stops growing. Counted over an exposure that grows with capability itself, the same assumptions return two thirds, not two, and cumulative burden is stricter again. The absolute rung (registration version 1.102, line 609) subtracts the correction elasticity from two rather than from one; its derivation is the registration’s and is not reproduced here.

7.5 Proposition B-5 (varying growth)

Proposition B-5. If burden is proportional to dC/dR\mathrm{d}C/\mathrm{d}R along an arbitrary smooth increasing path, then WW is proportional to αRC/R\alpha_R C/R and not to C/RC/R, and with correction proportional to CχC^{\chi} at constant χ\chi, Δbal=1−αR(1−χ)−dln⁡αR/dln⁡R,\begin{equation*} \Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} = 1 - \alpha_R(1 - \chi) - \mathrm{d}\ln\alpha_R/\mathrm{d}\ln R, \end{equation*}(20) which is registration version 1.102, line 623 in symbols (“the trend of the correction-to-burden ratio is one, less the local elasticity multiplied by the correction shortfall, less the trend of the local elasticity itself”).

The last term vanishes throughout a range of depth only where αR\alpha_R is constant on that range, that is only for a power law there, where Δbal=1−α(1−χ)\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} = 1 - \alpha(1 - \chi); at a single depth it vanishes wherever αR\alpha_R is stationary, which a path that is not a power law can reach: ln⁡(C/C0)=(ln⁡(R/R0))3/3+ln⁡(R/R0)\ln(C/C_0) = (\ln(R/R_0))^3/3 + \ln(R/R_0) has αR=1+(ln⁡(R/R0))2\alpha_R = 1 + (\ln(R/R_0))^2, stationary at R=R0R = R_0. Otherwise the general chain rule must carry the dependence inside WW or carry αR\alpha_R as an extra state variable. Merely replacing a constant α\alpha by αR\alpha_R in the simplified ceiling loses this term.

7.6 Proposition B-6 (sensitivities, the gap identity, and what an intervention does)

Proposition B-6. With the other quantities fixed, dαbaldη=1κ−χ;dαbaldχ=η−ζ(κ−χ)2;dαbaldκ=−η−ζ(κ−χ)2;dαbaldζ=−1κ−χ.\begin{equation*} \frac{\mathrm{d}\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}}{\mathrm{d}\eta} = \frac{1}{\kappa - \chi}; \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}}{\mathrm{d}\chi} = \frac{\eta - \zeta}{(\kappa - \chi)^2}; \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}}{\mathrm{d}\kappa} = -\frac{\eta - \zeta}{(\kappa - \chi)^2}; \quad \frac{\mathrm{d}\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}}}{\mathrm{d}\zeta} = -\frac{1}{\kappa - \chi}. \end{equation*}(21) So raising η\eta raises the ceiling when κ>χ\kappa > \chi, and raising χ\chi raises it only when η−ζ>0\eta - \zeta > 0. In the pacing case at fixed η\eta, the build-order gap is αcrit(first)−αcrit(after)=(χfirst−χafter)αcrit(first)αcrit(after)/(1+η)\begin{equation*} \alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}(\mathrm{first}) - \alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}(\mathrm{after}) = (\chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}})\,\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}(\mathrm{first})\,\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}}(\mathrm{after})/(1 + \eta) \end{equation*}(22) in the positive-ceiling domain. In the same pacing case, with κ=1\kappa = 1 and ζ=−1\zeta = -1 in both arms, where a placement contrast moves both terms, in-loop placement raises the boundary if and only if (1+ηin)/(1+ηout)>(1−χin)/(1−χout),\begin{equation*} (1 + \eta_{\mathrm{in}})/(1 + \eta_{\mathrm{out}}) > (1 - \chi_{\mathrm{in}})/(1 - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}), \end{equation*}(23) with 1−χ>01 - \chi > 0 and 1+η>01 + \eta > 0 in both arms.

Equation (22) reads χ\chi as an elasticity of correction capacity. A contrast measured as misalignment removed per pass on a fixed fault set moves the boundary through equation (22) only under a stated removal law, which the deciding instrument names. One favourable term alone is insufficient, and an intervention that also raises burden can lower the boundary. Outside the pacing case the comparison is between the two arms’ balance roots, each with its own burden elasticities, and the pacing condition does not carry over: with κ=2\kappa = 2 and ζ=−1\zeta = -1 in both arms, (χ,η)=(1/2,1/5)(\chi, \eta) = (1/2, 1/5) in the loop and (2/5,3/10)(2/5, 3/10) outside it, the pacing condition holds, yet the in-loop root is 4/54/5 and the other 13/1613/16, so in-loop placement lowers the boundary. These are algebraic regimes, not safety conclusions: the trend is not the level (registration version 1.102, line 625: “this quantity says whether the ratio is IMPROVING, never whether it EXCEEDS ONE.”), and Q/W=R/100Q/W = R/100 improves throughout R∈[1,10]R \in [1, 10] while staying below one. Trend, level, backlog and event stay distinct.

Local elasticities throughout make this a local boundary; a boundary written as a function of the architecture (whose letter for the architecture is one of the eight colliding symbols and is not printed; its root reads every elasticity, the burden’s included, in the architecture) is the statement that changing the arm changes the arm’s elasticities and so moves αbal\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} through these sensitivities; it is written here per arm without an architecture symbol, and where the burden elasticities also differ between arms the comparison is the general one above.

The ARC Bound reading.

The Bound is the same-class value of the pacing model at χ=1/2\chi = 1/2 and η=0\eta = 0, not a fourth or sixth law. A control stands: a study quoting the simple form declares the corrector’s direct depth-dependence before the run and shows it near zero by an equivalence result with a pre-fixed band whose upper edge is at most half the margin the deciding instrument registers for the profile maximum; a wider band, or a missing demonstration, is NOT EVALUABLE for the Bound reading, never survival. That margin is not yet a number: P3’s tolerance “is the author’s to fix” and until then P3’s supported outcome and this control are NOT EVALUABLE (registration version 1.102, line 843), which Section 10 records. No numerical band is chosen here; P3’s statement, refuter (registration version 1.102, line 851) and scoring are unchanged, and a positive η\eta asserted after a run never excuses a P3 exceedance.

The Boundary Transfer (the report’s own models; not registered).

A held-out prediction of the balance transition from independently estimated elasticities inherits their precision. The registration reports the growth exponent’s re-estimate as approximately 0.49, one model’s fit, a regression estimate with a standard error of 0.20, and the 95 per cent interval [−1.3,2.9][-1.3, 2.9] as the bootstrap interval on the same row’s endpoint estimate of 0.59 (registration version 1.102, line 207, which also calls the re-estimate robust, a word version 1.104 drops); that interval’s positive part contains αcrit=2\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 2, on the relative rung, at the registered dials, and Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} is positive at either point estimate and negative at 2.9, so no transfer prediction built on it has a decided sign; the non-positive part of the interval lies outside the burden model, whose burden must be positive. A transfer unit therefore carries its own precision gate, fixed before the transition data are opened: the half-width of the predicted boundary’s interval small against the band the boundary-mapping unit registers for the boundary location, the registered standard error of its estimator (registration version 1.102, lines 621 and 633); it is an unregistered study, not law content.

7.7 Proposition B-7 (the capability coordinate)

Proposition B-7. Let capability be re-expressed by an increasing differentiable map whose local elasticity, the derivative of the logarithm of the new coordinate in the logarithm of the old, is positive throughout. Read in the new coordinate, the growth elasticity αR\alpha_R is multiplied by that elasticity, χ\chi and κ\kappa are divided by it, and η\eta, ζ\zeta and Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} are unchanged; so κ−χ\kappa - \chi keeps its sign, αbal\alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} is multiplied by the same elasticity, the verdict αR<αbal\alpha_R < \alpha_{\mathrm{bal}} is unchanged, and every contrast of capability elasticities between arms at a common capability (χfirst−χafter\chi_{\mathrm{first}} - \chi_{\mathrm{after}}, χin−χout\chi_{\mathrm{in}} - \chi_{\mathrm{out}}) is divided by it. (Proof: Appendix A.16.)

Signs, ceilings against floors and every verdict on the balance are therefore free of the coordinate, and numbers are not: on the squared coordinate, C2C^2, an order contrast of 0.15 is 0.075, below P12’s minimum effect. The registration fixes the numbers on one scale: “Every numerical exponent and every exponent-scale margin in this registration is stated on the scale this condition fixes and on no other” (registration version 1.102, line 403, Condition B), and for the same-class value, “THE BOUND IS FIXED ON ONE CAPABILITY SCALE AND ON NO OTHER” (registration version 1.102, line 935). αcrit=1/(1−χ)\alpha_{\mathrm{crit}} = 1/(1 - \chi), the ARC Bound’s two on the relative rung, the same-class value one half, P12’s minimum effect 0.10 and the genesis reading’s margin are numbers on that scale. A meaningful zero and an uncapped range, which the registration gives its ladder scale (registration version 1.102, line 259), do not by themselves fix it: every positive power of CC keeps both and multiplies the growth elasticity by the power, so the justification Condition B requires must also exclude power re-expressions. The registered burden model’s values are themselves values on that scale (on C2C^2, κ=1\kappa = 1 becomes one half), so re-expressing capability alone and reapplying 1/(1−χ)1/(1 - \chi) shows nothing: with α=9/5\alpha = 9/5 and χ=9/20\chi = 9/20 the bound is 20/1120/11 on CC; on C2C^2, α=18/5\alpha = 18/5, χ=9/40\chi = 9/40 and κ=1/2\kappa = 1/2 give 40/1140/11, and the verdict stands, while 1/(1−9/40)=40/311/(1 - 9/40) = 40/31 would reverse it. One inconsistency of the frozen registration bears on Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, and is carried to the successor registration (Section 10, item 15): registration version 1.102, line 403 states every exponent-scale margin on Condition B’s scale, but Condition B’s lists (registration version 1.102, lines 409 and 415) leave P12 out, and Condition E2 (registration version 1.102, line 421) names P12 among the predictions that return “no correction exponent”, although P12’s endpoint is “the quantity the third law’s ceiling is written in” (registration version 1.102, line 1039); P12’s 0.10 rests on Condition B’s scale through registration version 1.102, line 403 alone.

7.8 Proposition B-8: the balance over a finite range of depth (the report’s own models; not registered)

Identity B-1 gives the trend of the ratio Q/WQ/W at a point. Over a range of depth it gives the change in the ratio’s level.

Proposition B-8. On one specified trajectory, with QQ and WW positive, in comparable units, on one clock and with one conversion fixed throughout, let 0<R1<R20 < R_1 < R_2 lie in the domain and let Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} be integrable in ln⁡R\ln R between them. Then ln⁡[Q(R2)/W(R2)]=ln⁡[Q(R1)/W(R1)]+∫R1R2Δbal(r)dln⁡r,\begin{equation*} \ln[Q(R_2)/W(R_2)] = \ln[Q(R_1)/W(R_1)] + \int_{R_1}^{R_2} \Delta_{\mathrm{bal}}(r)\,\mathrm{d}\ln r, \end{equation*}(24) where Q(r)Q(r) and W(r)W(r) are read along that trajectory and rr is the variable of integration. (Proof: Appendix A.17.)

So the level at the start of a range is part of any prediction of the level at its end, and the trend alone predicts neither. For a constant trend Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} other than zero, on a trajectory anchored at R0R_0, the ratio is Q(R)/W(R)=[Q(R0)/W(R0)](R/R0)ΔbalQ(R)/W(R) = [Q(R_0)/W(R_0)]\,(R/R_0)^{\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}}}, and it meets one at R⋆=R0[W(R0)/Q(R0)]1/Δbal.\begin{equation*} R_\star = R_0\,[W(R_0)/Q(R_0)]^{1/\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}}}. \end{equation*}(25)

With a positive trend the crossing lies beyond the anchor exactly when Q(R0)<W(R0)Q(R_0) < W(R_0): where service already exceeds burden at the anchor the expression returns a depth before it, and where the two are equal it returns the anchor. With a negative trend the same expression gives the depth at which the ratio falls through one, which lies beyond the anchor exactly when Q(R0)>W(R0)Q(R_0) > W(R_0). With a zero trend the ratio keeps its starting level throughout. R⋆R_\star is a formal crossing: nothing in it shows that the depth lies inside the range measured, or inside any range a system can reach. Nor does a ratio above one bound a backlog, a transient error or a harm; trend, level, backlog and event stay distinct (Section 7.6).
