A prediction made with this proposition therefore records in advance the levels at the anchor with their uncertainty, the range of depth it covers, the clock and the conversion, and the separately measured outcome it is meant to reach; and none of these is chosen with the held-out observation in view.

The coordinate.

Proposition B-7 governs any change of the capability coordinate, and the power case shows the pattern: where capability is re-expressed so that its ratio to its reference value becomes (C/C0)p(C/C_0)^p with p>0p > 0, αR\alpha_R becomes pαRp\alpha_R, χ\chi becomes χ/p\chi/p and κ\kappa becomes κ/p\kappa/p, while η\eta, ζ\zeta and Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} are unchanged, and so is the integral above. To change the coordinate and keep the old number for the burden’s capability elasticity is to change the model (Section 7.7). Every numerical threshold on an exponent, P12’s minimum effect among them, stays on the scale Condition B fixes. Nothing in this proposition replaces the ARC Co-Scaling Law’s criterion, that βC\beta_C exceeds kk, or removes an identification on which Law III, the ARC Ceiling, rests.

7.9 What a new deciding instrument declares (the report’s own models; not registered)

A new instrument that reads correction service against burden declares each of the following before any of its outcomes is read. The list is stated here (the report’s own models; not registered) as a condition of such an instrument’s completeness; it amends no frozen unit.

Table 3. What a new deciding instrument declares before any of its outcomes is read (the report’s own models; not registered).
It declares So that this is settled in advance
The system’s state, and what may change in it code, weights, tools, memory, permissions, the state of training and the mechanism of update; a loop that runs inference on fixed weights is described as that
Capability as measured: its zero, scale and range the case for a ratio scale, with a reason that excludes power re-expressions, the calibration, any floor or ceiling of the measure, and which changes of coordinate are allowed (Section 7.7); the balance exponent, which no change of coordinate moves, printed beside every number stated on the scale; and the readings under the plausible alternative scales
Depth, and the clock on which service and burden are read how rounds are counted, the reference values, the unit of exposure, and any conversion between clocks with its uncertainty
What is counted as correction capacity available, corrections attempted, corrections delivered and the net change in error, each kept apart; and whether the workload offered limited what could be delivered
What is counted as burden the same unit of exposure and the same clock as correction, with any conversion justified before Q/WQ/W is formed
The units of observation, and which are independent systems, training replicates, model families, checkpoints and repeated items, with the dependence among them kept in the analysis
The intervention and the estimand whether capability is assigned or attained; whether the quantity is a total effect or a contrast at fixed capability (Section 6.4); the range the arms share; and the error of measurement on each axis
The model and its primary contrasts an intercept and both slopes for every cell, or the equivalent full set of interactions (Section 6.4), with the order contrast and the placement contrast named
The decision rule and its uncertainty the registered endpoint, the smallest effect of interest, the joint interval, and the rules for missing data, for zeros and for stopping
The planner, where one is studied its complete objective, horizon, feasible family and permitted early stops, its discounting and selection tolerance, and how coverage and realisation are checked (Section 5.5)

The claim fixes the measurement, never the reverse. P12 is read on its undirected contrast in the correction-leverage exponent, on the registered axis. P21 is read on its behavioural outcome, the interaction of placement with depth, within its registered access and action-space design. P15 is read on the retained fraction of an externally installed gain after later capability training, and P23 on the difference of two retained fractions, the embedded arm’s less the external arm’s, under later training of the same kind. A ratio of correction service, a behavioural gain at one fixed budget, or a comparison of retained fractions on another scale or under another kind of later training is none of these four endpoints and is never scored in place of one. A mediation hypothesis is a candidate for a registration of its own, and it is not part of a successor to version 1.102 until it has been reviewed and given an instrument. Version 1.103 registers two directional readings without changing these endpoints: the ARC Embedding Law’s build-order limb reads P12’s interval with a direction P12 does not carry, and P21’s directional reading scores no widening of the registered size, or a narrowing, against P21 (Sections 6.1 and 6.6).

8 Dependencies, logical separation and conventions

  1. Register dependencies (the statement paper’s dependency table, Eastwood 2026h, in its section 2a): ARC-1’s failure does not refute the persistence registers; ARC-2 depends on ARC-1’s measurables, not its verdict, and its failure takes ARC-3’s derivation; ARC-3’s failure does not erase ARC-2’s own result. The ARC Persistence Law’s objects need no growth law; the ARC Embedding Law’s two limbs need none; only Law V’s boundary reading depends on the ARC Ceiling’s model and through it on ARC-2, and it needs the same system and admissible scopes. The registration (Eastwood 2026j) reads that table’s rows at the width of its registered lines, narrowing the row for ARC-2 and the row for ARC-4 before any data (registration version 1.105, the ARC Ceiling’s word and the ARC Embedding Law’s dependence on ARC-4).

  2. Logical separation, at the level of verdicts. The registration states it: “The laws are untouched.” (registration version 1.102, line 1087, for P15) and “The three laws are untouched” (registration version 1.102, line 1237, for P21). The registration reads the untouched laws of P21’s entry as Laws I, II and III (registration version 1.105, the qualifications to the entries of P21 and P15), since Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, are not untouched by failures of their own carriers, and under it a P15 refutation refutes Law IV through its retention limb (Section 5.8), so the laws these lines call untouched are Laws I to III. The ARC Ceiling’s relation holds at every value of χ\chi, so any P12 verdict, which is a contrast in the very symbol Law III’s equation is written in (registration version 1.102, line 1039: “the quantity the third law’s ceiling is written in”), is consistent with it; separation is independence of truth values, not absence of the symbol. Three listed models make it concrete, each at the registered dials (χ=1/2\chi = 1/2, η=0\eta = 0, κ=1\kappa = 1, ζ=−1\zeta = -1) with a growth exponent of 3/23/2, so that the growth exponent lies below the ceiling of two and the balance exponent is positive, Δbal=1/4\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} = 1/4: (a) an interval on Sext(1)S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1) from 0.85 to 0.95, which would refute P15 and so the ARC Persistence Law’s retention limb, and with it Law IV; (b) an interval on the build-order change in the exponent lying inside P12’s open tolerance band, and an interval on the placement-by-depth interaction on the outcome lying inside the tolerance registered with P21’s instrument, each from a design meeting its sensitivity clause, so that both registered refuters would fire and both limbs of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, would be struck; (c) an interval on Sext(1)S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1) from 0.2 to 0.4 with the intervals of model (b), under which Law IV’s retention limb would be supported, the law staying under test, while both limbs of Law V would be struck. Across the three the verdicts on P12, P15 and P21 vary while the dials, and every statement of Sections 7.1 to 7.4 about them, stay fixed. The dials do not by themselves establish Laws I to III, each a law under test: Law I, the ARC Principle, is a claim about measured growth, and the ARC Co-Scaling Law’s criterion compares βC\beta_C with kk, which the registration does not identify with this model’s elasticities (Section 7.3). Model (b) is written on the registered endpoints because P21 decides an interaction on the outcome, “never a measurement of an exponent” (registration version 1.102, line 1221), and its refuter reads that interaction (registration version 1.102, line 1227); read on the service surfaces instead, ηin=ηout\eta_{\mathrm{in}} = \eta_{\mathrm{out}} would make GembG_{\mathrm{emb}} constant in depth along a growing path only together with χin=χout\chi_{\mathrm{in}} = \chi_{\mathrm{out}} (Identity V-1), and its constancy is not what fires P21’s refuter. These are separations of statements, not empirical findings. A countermodel put forward for the case in which Laws I to III hold while Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, fails takes a collapse, SV(x)=exp⁡(−10x)S_V(x) = \exp(-10x), which on the external arm would support P15; it reads the failure of Law IV in the comparative sense of Section 5.6, the opposite direction from model (a), which is one more reason the comparative content was kept apart from P15’s face; version 1.103 registered it as the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb, without a proposition, and version 1.105 registers that limb’s proposition, P23 (Section 5.1). Two registered links are recorded rather than left to be found: registration version 1.102, line 663 carries Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, “by P4, with P7 asking what class deployed correction actually belongs to, and P12 and P15 asking whether placement and subsequent training move it”; and registration version 1.102, line 667 holds the ARC Ceiling’s relation only where “the direct depth term is zero”, which the mechanism reading ηo,in>ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} > \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}} denies in at least one placement, so that where that reading holds Law III’s simple form, and the ARC Bound read from it, apply in at most one placement; that link is confined to the boundary reading and to the η\eta term of the Bound-reading control, and a P20 verdict is scored in ARC-3 alone.

  3. The register convention (set out by version 0.2.1; not in force; version 1.103’s dependence takes its place). Version 0.2.1 set out, as a grouping fixed in advance and not as an entailment, that on an evaluable P15 refutation Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, be withdrawn whole, and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, with it as a law of the theory; that Law V’s refutation not withdraw Law IV; and that P12 and P21 keep their own measured verdicts. Two published statements stood behind it, and they are different statements. The registration ties a P15 refutation to “this programme’s case that correction has to sit inside the system rather than be applied to it from outside” (registration version 1.102, line 1085). The statement paper’s dependency table has “ARC-4 falls and takes ARC-5 with it”, and the trigger of that fall in the same paper is the comparative observation of its kill sentence (Section 5.6), not P15. Nothing in ηo,in>ηo,out\eta_{o,\mathrm{in}} > \eta_{o,\mathrm{out}} or in the P12 endpoint is entailed by any value of Sext(1)S_{\mathrm{ext}}(1). Version 1.103 fixed the dependence before any data, as a registered dependence and not an entailment, at the narrower of the paper’s two widths: Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is struck only by a refuted verdict on the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb, once a later successor has registered that limb’s entry; a refuted P15 alone refutes Law IV and leaves Law V to its own limbs; until the comparison limb is registered no result on ARC-4 strikes Law V; and a Law V struck in this way is printed as refuted, struck by its registered dependence on that comparison, with the unit and the date, while P12 and P21 keep the marks they earned (registration version 1.105, Law V’s dependence on ARC-4). It narrows the paper’s table row and its note of 3 October 2026, “where ARC-4 falls, ARC-5 falls with it”, to that form. Version 1.105 gives the dependence its entry: the refuted verdict that strikes Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is a refuted P23, an inconclusive, untested or NOT EVALUABLE P23 strikes nothing, and a refuted P15 alone still leaves Law V to its own limbs (registration version 1.105, the dependence’s entry).

  4. No P12, P15 or P21 verdict automatically refutes another numbered proposition. P19’s refutation removes ARC-5’s motivation and refutes nothing in it (registration version 1.102, line 111). P13 stays outside the laws.

  5. The Eden Protocol is a method, not a law, and is not entailed by these laws: “It follows from no law here, it is carried jointly by P12, P13, P15 and P21, with P7 as its premise and P19 as its motivation, and it can fail while every law stands or stand while they fall.” (registration version 1.102, line 61); its endogeneity condition is tested by the method’s own registrations and no verdict here turns on it (registration version 1.102, line 675). Its success criterion is a formation criterion, not a later-conduct criterion. The registration reads the laws of that sentence as Laws I, II and III, since three of the Protocol’s four carriers now also carry Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, and the Protocol remains a method, not a consequence of any law (registration version 1.105, its qualification of the method’s separability). Version 1.105 makes P23 a fifth carrier of the method’s endogeneity condition, with P12, P13, P15 and P21, so that if those five fail the Protocol’s engineering recommendation fails with them, and Laws I to III are untouched (registration version 1.105, a fifth carrier). The Honey Architecture (Paper VI, Eastwood 2026c) is likewise outside every verdict here.

  6. The flagship conjunction P1, P4, P16, P20, P21 stands as registered (registration version 1.102, line 763); a surviving subset is not the conjunction.

  7. A persistence advantage and a favourable elasticity contrast are separate: an architecture can preserve a property with no favourable contrast, or improve scaling while losing it; a positive retention comparison alone is not causal mediation (Section 9).

9 The register of unregistered objects

Each entry is a proposition or object this document states beyond the registered propositions, and each carries the label the report’s own models; not registered, printed in parentheses after its name wherever it is stated, or, in the title of a numbered result, after the name inside the title’s own parentheses, as “the report’s own models, not registered”: the object is this report’s own mathematics, model, reporting rule or requirement, no registration fixes it, and none is law content until the author registers it. Version 1.103 (Eastwood 2026j) registers, as the laws’ own words, the build-order limb’s direction with the genesis reading’s strike rule, the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb, which names the comparison IV-PERSIST writes, and verdict rules for both laws that take the place of the law-level clauses this document set out; version 1.105 registers that limb’s proposition, P23, on the difference this section rules primary (registration version 1.105, P23, its fourth fixed thing). Ruling on the ΛV\Lambda_V mediation bridge.

Adopted (the report’s own models; not registered), with this status line: “Mediation contrast (the report’s own models; not registered); not law content; ΛV:=ln⁡(Semb/Sext)\Lambda_V := \ln(S_{\mathrm{emb}}/S_{\mathrm{ext}}) at the evaluation budget, defined only where both retentions are positive; the primary contrast is the difference Semb(x)−Sext(x)S_{\mathrm{emb}}(x) - S_{\mathrm{ext}}(x), which is defined wherever both retained fractions are established, whatever their signs, with ΛV\Lambda_V reported beside it where defined; neither is defined without the embedded arm, and both need the measurement of Section 5.6.1; instrument: a unit registered in a scope that carries both the retention contrast and the elasticity contrasts, since P15’s unit is governed by S5 (registration version 1.102, line 237) and P12 and P21 by S7 (registration version 1.102, line 239), and no proposition may borrow a scope (registration version 1.102, lines 241 and 247), so a retention contrast read on the registered two-arm unit (registration version 1.102, line 1089) alone is an S5 quantity that bears on no ARC-5 proposition; a positive value is not mediation: the mediating sequence stated here, embedding to the elasticity contrasts to Δbal\Delta_{\mathrm{bal}} to a persistence advantage, has three links, each needing its own identified estimate, and each link can fail; the adverse margin, multiplicity and registration are the author’s.” Reasons. It is adopted rather than declined on its merits: it is the one object in the set that would connect the two registers once one system is registered in a scope that carries both contrasts. It is stated on the difference scale first because the log form is undefined on a region the data can reach (where one retention is negative and the other positive, or where either is zero), and because where both retentions are negative the log form is defined but its sign is the reverse of the difference’s. A dilution common to the two arms, such as weight decay towards a common reference, multiplies both retained fractions by one factor: it leaves their ratio, and ΛV\Lambda_V, unchanged and shrinks their difference by that factor (Section 5.9). A margin fixed on the difference therefore reads placement and common dilution together; an instrument that fixes its margin there reports ΛV\Lambda_V beside it, with an arm that measures the common factor. It is one object with IV-PERSIST, so that one test does not become two propositions. Nothing states that the loop is closed. Version 1.103 registered the ARC Persistence Law’s comparison limb, which names the comparison this contrast reads, without a proposition, and its entry, P23, fixes the margin and the scale: the difference decides, at a margin of 0.10, and the logarithm of the ratio, ΛV\Lambda_V’s value where both fractions are positive, is printed beside it and never decides (registration version 1.105, P23, its fourth fixed thing; Section 5.1).

Two things follow for the successor registrations. A result on the difference and a result on ΛV\Lambda_V are one result, not two corroborations. And ΛV\Lambda_V as a mediation contrast entered no registered version: version 1.105 registers the difference as P23’s endpoint and calls the mediation contrast unregistered, so ΛV\Lambda_V, its margins and any instrument for it are candidates for a registration of their own (registration version 1.105, P23, what a supported result does not establish; Section 10, item 9).

10 Open questions

There are fifteen questions in all, numbered as version 1.1 numbered them. Where an item names a default, that default stands until the author says otherwise, and none is chosen after a result. Version 1.103 (Eastwood 2026j), registered on 15 October 2026, has since settled items 3, 4, 5 and 10, and items 1, 2, 13, 14 and 15 in part, and version 1.105, registered on 18 November 2026, settles item 8 in part and more of items 1 and 15; each such item says what the registration fixed and what stays open, and the version 1.1 wording of the items version 1.103 reached is kept in Appendix B.4. The other items stay open as written.

  1. The ARC Persistence Law’s content. Settled in part by version 1.103: Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, has two limbs, the retention limb, P15’s registered claim word for word, and the comparison limb. Version 1.105 registers that limb’s entry, P23: its operational definition of correction embedded in the training objective, its concurrent baseline, its margin of 0.10, its scale, the difference, and the embedded arm’s own fraction printed and never required to clear one half, decided only under later training of the same kind (Section 5.1); the comparison under later training of another kind has no registered proposition. The loss mechanism, active removal against dilution, stays unresolved for real systems; the training model of Section 5.9 separates the two inside a model, removal acting direction by direction at rates the later loss sets and dilution acting on both arms alike.

  2. What a P15 refutation takes from Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law. Settled in part by version 1.103: a refuted retention limb refutes Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, read against a baseline arm named in advance, above a floor fixed in advance and under the attestation, and the law is then printed refuted with the proposition, the unit, the date and whose run it was (Section 5.8). Of the four controls version 0.2.1 set out, the capability rise established on a separate instrument is not among the registered conditions (registration version 1.105, Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, kill condition and verdict rule) and stays open.

  3. The register convention. Settled by version 1.103: Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is struck through Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, only by a refuted verdict on Law IV’s comparison limb, which from version 1.105 is a refuted P23, and a refuted P15 alone leaves Law V to its own limbs (Section 8, item 3).

  4. Whether Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is severable by limb, a strict conjunction, or stands on the placement limb alone. Settled by version 1.103: Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is refuted when either limb’s own verdict is refuted, or when its dependence strikes it, and supported only when both limbs are supported (Section 6.6).

Settled by version 1.103, which reads the placement limb on P21’s own verdict, the registered access interaction and the default here, and prints P21’s mechanism axis beside it (Section 6.1); the service-scaling mechanism reading of registration version 1.102, line 1239 would need a separately specified bridge and design, never a rescoring.

11 What this paper does and does not show

Status.

Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, were added on 24 September 2026 and registered as laws on 15 October 2026 by version 1.103 of the theory registration (Eastwood 2026j), each with its statement, its kill condition and its verdict rule fixed before any data that could decide it. Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, carries P15 and P23, in register ARC-4, P23 the entry of its comparison limb; Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, carries P12 (undirected) and P21, in register ARC-5, and reads its build-order limb on P12’s interval with a direction P12 does not carry; P12, P15 and P21 were registered on 8 September 2026 and P23 on 18 November 2026 (Section 3.2). Each law is a law under test. Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, is not yet tested. Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, remains a law under test: its placement limb, P21, is supported on the performance axis only, under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism, and one disclosed recovery amendment; its build-order limb, read on P12, is undecided, since P12 is untested. That run is Unit 83, registered on 22 October 2026 (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/MN73W, Eastwood 2026i) and run on 27 and 28 October 2026 (results: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/98HKR). Today one limb has a registered instrument that has run: P21, the placement limb of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law (Unit 83); a second registered test of it, on three providers, has not yet run (Unit 83b, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/4HK32). P15, P23 and P12 have no instrument, so Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, cannot yet be supported, and the build-order limb of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, can be neither supported nor struck. The programme’s first registered study, Unit 06, a classification audit that tests no law, was registered on 1 October 2026 (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/RV2B5; Eastwood 2026k) and ran on 6 October 2026; it is reported in full as administratively incomplete, with no verdict claimed (results: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/4BPHG). Version 1.3 added the hypotheses version 1.2 left unstated, the scope of Theorems IV-G and IV-H, a minimal training model for Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, and two minimal models for Law V, the ARC Embedding Law. This version, 1.4, adds the premise Proposition V-4(c) needs and the range Proposition V-4(e)’s reading needs, corrects how Section 7.3 reaches the criterion of Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, and reads the registration at version 1.105: its theorems are proved under the assumptions each states, its identities are checked, and Section 10 lists fifteen questions, eleven of them still open in whole or in part. Theorems IV-G, IV-H, IV-S and IV-C, Corollaries IV-G′', IV-H′' and IV-C′', Lemmas IV-K and IV-M′' and Propositions IV-N, IV-R, IV-L, IV-U, V-4 and V-5 are logical proofs, not identities; no proof assistant is used, and they rest on the written proofs, which finite models exercise and do not replace.

What kind of document this is.

This document is not a registration, not an empirical result, and not authority to run any study. Registration versions 1.100, 1.102, 1.103, 1.104 and 1.105 stay frozen byte for byte; Laws I to III stand exactly as registered (registration version 1.102, lines 659, 663 and 665); no proposition is added to or moved between registers; P12 keeps no direction; and every object this document introduces beyond the registered propositions and the laws’ registered words is marked (the report’s own models; not registered), the label Section 9 defines, and is not law content until the author registers it. Where version 1.103 or version 1.105 registered an object this document had stated, the object is marked as registered by that version where it stands (Section 9).

What this document is.

The mathematics of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law (register ARC-4, carrying P15 and P23), and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law (register ARC-5, carrying P12 and P21): the objects, the conditional theorems with proofs, the identities that connect the two laws to the registered balance model, the registered faces quoted byte for byte, and the kill conditions. The register assignment is that of registration version 1.102, line 99 (“ARC-4, VALUE PERSISTENCE: P15 alone.” and “ARC-5, THE GENESIS STRATEGY: P12 and P21.”), with P23 placed in ARC-4 by version 1.105; the seven propositions in no register are those of registration version 1.102, line 101 (P5, P7, P10, P11, P13, P14, P19), and they stay there.

What it is not.

It proves no empirical law: algebra proves consequences of assumptions, not that real systems satisfy them. It runs no test. It adds no registered proposition and moves none. It does not restate Laws I to III (Section 9). It supplies no missing measurement and chooses no scientific parameter the author has held (Section 10). Section 2 names the nearest earlier work found and says what each states; where a search was made, its date and scope stand with the result it concerns (Sections 5.9 and 6.8).

Safety and usefulness.

No safety measure is stated here, so none is paired with a usefulness measure: Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, says what persists, not that what persists is good, and Sections 5.7 and 6.7 say what the mathematics does not show.

12 Limitations

The limits below are the report’s own, each stated where it arises; they are gathered here so that none is missed.

  • Conditional mathematics. Every theorem, lemma and proposition holds under the premises it states, and the report shows for no real system that those premises hold (Section 11). Nothing in Sections 5 to 7 has been measured.

  • Proofs and checks. The proofs are written proofs. No proof assistant is used; finite models exercise the proofs and do not replace them, and the computer-algebra checks of the identities and the second check of the working draft are the programme’s own, not independent verification (Appendix B).

  • The minimal models. The training model of Section 5.9 is local and quadratic, with one curvature and an affine property score, and Theorem IV-C holds only under Assumption S; the two models of Section 6.8 rest on the premises they name. Each says what a test must measure, and none is evidence for either law.

  • The margins are defined, not computed. The strategic viability margin is a supremum over a feasible family that cannot be enumerated for a real system, and it presupposes a known objective; where the objective is unknown it is NOT EVALUABLE, and no incomplete search confirms a positive margin (Section 5.5).

  • Identification. The capability elasticity of correction service is the registered correction-leverage exponent only under the conditions of Section 4; the local elasticities are identified only where capability is assigned or a no-confounding premise is stated in advance (Section 6.4); and the identification of the ARC Co-Scaling Law’s βC\beta_C with χ\chi is unestablished (Section 7.3).

  • Scale. Exponent numbers, P12’s minimum effect among them, hold only on the capability scale condition B fixes; signs and verdicts on the balance do not depend on the coordinate, and numbers do (Section 7.7).

  • Earlier work. Section 2 names the nearest earlier work found and says what each states. Where this report says that a result was not found stated, the search’s date and scope stand with it (Sections 5.9 and 6.8); it makes no other statement about novelty.

  • Representations. What persists when a rewrite changes the system’s own representations is not treated here: the property’s score would then need a map from the successor’s representations to the observables it is scored on, one that keeps the property, and how such a map is verified is an open problem, named here and not solved.

  • Open questions. Section 10 records fifteen questions; those still open include the budget scale and the at-the-margin band for P15, the baseline a unit that decides P15 alone takes and the floor’s value, P3’s tolerance, and P12’s listing under conditions B and E2. Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, cannot be supported until instruments decide P15 and P23.

13 Conclusion

Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law, are registered laws under test, and this report gives them their mathematics. The ARC Persistence Law’s retention limb is read on one quantity, the retained fraction of an externally installed gain at the matched budget, and the report states what that fraction needs before it can decide P15. Persistence of a property over a finite horizon follows, under stated premises, from greedy acceptance with a margin or from planned optimisation with a strategic viability margin, and each premise names the observation that would refute it. Neither mechanism reaches later training by gradient steps; in the smallest model of that training, an installed gain fades at the rates the later loss’s curvature sets along it, and, under later training of the same kind, a gain installed with the capability loss in the objective fades no faster than one installed afterwards. The ARC Embedding Law’s limbs are read on P12’s interval, with the direction version 1.103 (Eastwood 2026j) registers, and on P21’s interaction of placement with depth; the balance identity shows how a change in the capability elasticity the build-order limb reads, or in the direct depth-dependence the placement limb’s mechanism reading names, would move the boundary inside the ARC Ceiling’s model, which stays unchanged. In the smallest model of each limb, the placement limb follows where uncorrected faults seed later ones or an outside checker’s detection falls with what it inspects, and the build-order limb follows only where what is formed first loses its coverage more slowly than a corrector added after falls behind, so each model names what its test must measure. None of this is a measurement. The laws take their words from their registered tests alone: P15’s retained fraction, P23’s difference of retained fractions under later training of the same kind, P12’s order contrast and P21’s interaction, each read as the registration says.

A.15 Moments of the error carried across rewrites

The moments and the convergence. Without the pull, V(n)−V(0)=∑t=1nerrtV^{(n)} - V^{(0)} = \sum_{t=1}^{n}\mathrm{err}_t, a sum of nn independent terms, with mean nbiasn\,\mathrm{bias} and variance nvarerrn\,\mathrm{var}_{\mathrm{err}}. With it, the departure depn:=V(n)−V(0)\mathrm{dep}_n := V^{(n)} - V^{(0)} obeys depn=(1−pull)depn−1+errn\mathrm{dep}_n = (1 - \mathrm{pull})\,\mathrm{dep}_{n-1} + \mathrm{err}_n with dep0=0\mathrm{dep}_0 = 0, so depn=∑t=1n(1−pull)n−terrt\mathrm{dep}_n = \sum_{t=1}^{n}(1 - \mathrm{pull})^{n-t}\,\mathrm{err}_t; its mean is bias∑j=0n−1(1−pull)j\mathrm{bias}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(1 - \mathrm{pull})^{j} and its variance varerr∑j=0n−1(1−pull)2j\mathrm{var}_{\mathrm{err}}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(1 - \mathrm{pull})^{2j}, the two geometric sums stated, each rising with nn to its limit. For independent errors whose variances have a finite sum, the partial sums of the centred errors form a martingale bounded in mean square, which converges almost surely; so the sum of the errors converges exactly where the sum of their means converges. ◻

B.1 Version 1.4, 22 November 2026

Version 1.4 is the report’s next version. It follows version 1.3 of 17 November 2026, which stays published as revision 3 of the report’s PDF on OSF.

Why it was made.

Version 1.105 of the theory registration, approved on OSF on 18 November 2026, registers P23, the entry of the comparison limb of Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, so that version 1.3’s account of the registered setting no longer matched the registration. Outside reviews read on 21 November 2026, each point checked at its source within the programme, found two results stated without a premise or a range they need, one connection to Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, made through the exponent of absolute growth where Paper X’s criterion uses that of fractional growth, and one limit of a frozen design that the report did not state; notes the author sent the same week raised questions about persistence across rewrites. Version 1.4 carries every verified fix in one version.

What changed.

  1. The registration at version 1.105. P23 is printed where the report states Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, and what each register carries (Sections 3.1, 3.2, 5.1 and 11, and Table 1). The comparison limb takes P23’s verdict, and the law can be supported only when P15 and P23 are both supported (Section 5.8); P23’s baseline, three arms and capability rise are recorded where the report states the measurement (Sections 5.6 and 5.6.1); a refuted P23 is the verdict that strikes Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, through its registered dependence (Sections 6.6 and 8); P23 is a fifth carrier of the Eden Protocol (Section 8, item 5); the open questions the registration now settles in part are marked (Section 10, items 1, 3, 8, 9 and 15); and the registration’s resolution of the two statements of the build-order limb’s refutation is recorded (Section 6.6, item 2). Wherever the report gives a registered rule’s words it now cites them where version 1.105 states them; a dated statement of what an earlier version held keeps that version.

  2. The weak ordering. Section 5.9 now says that Theorem IV-C orders the two arms only weakly, with equality where either curvature is the same in every direction the property depends on, and that P23’s margin of 0.10 is the registration’s empirical prediction and no consequence of the theorem.

  3. Proposition V-4. Part (c) now requires 0<δin0 < \delta_{\mathrm{in}}, which it needs: at δin=0\delta_{\mathrm{in}} = 0 the ratio is constant, there is no turning depth and the difference falls at every depth, as the part now says; its proof and the notation entry carry the condition. The arrivals setting now bounds the score of an entry kept out, −1≤yk≤1-1 \le y_{\mathrm{k}} \le 1, which the reading of part (e) needs: outside that range a falling rejection of sound work can widen the lead (Section 6.8).

  4. Section 7.3. Version 1.3 connected the criterion of Law II, the ARC Co-Scaling Law, to the ceiling of Law III, the ARC Ceiling, by giving the burden model’s exponent (α−1)/α(\alpha - 1)/\alpha as the kk of Paper X, whose kk is the exponent of fractional growth. On the depth clock that exponent is −1/α-1/\alpha, the relative criterion does not give the ceiling, and the reciprocal form comes from Paper X’s absolute criterion; the section now says so, places the registration’s drift exponent as that kk plus one, and states the rule for a change of clock. The identification βC=χ\beta_C = \chi stays unestablished.

  5. Unit 83’s monitor. Section 6.5 states one limit of the frozen design of Unit 83, the counted test of in-loop correction with depth, that bears on reading its widening, with the descriptive split that Unit 83b’s registration records.

  6. The label. The label UNREGISTERED is now written (the report’s own models; not registered) after a name, and in a numbered result’s title after the name inside the title’s own parentheses, as Section 9 defines once; the meaning is unchanged.

  7. Weighed and added. Section 5.5.1 models error carried across rewrites, a random walk where each rewrite is judged by the values then held and a bounded departure where rewrites are pulled back towards a retained reference, with its derivation in Appendix A.15; Section 6.4 rules that a design with a handful of model families treats family as a fixed stratum; the list of Section 7.9 asks for the reason that excludes power re-expressions of capability, the balance exponent beside every number stated on the scale and the readings under alternative scales; and Section 12 names, as an open problem, what persists when a rewrite changes the system’s representations.

  8. Earlier work. Five passages now say only what the parts of the works read carry. In Section 2, one measured advantage is said to widen with the number of sampled solutions searched, not with depth, and two works that could not be read at source are credited with what their titles name, as their references now say; two passages that named the source of the ratio interval where the report states its own result now name the interval alone (Sections 5.6.1 and 9), the source’s reference saying that its abstract was read.

  9. The first page. The abstract states P23’s prediction beside P15’s, within its limit.

  10. What the embedding mathematics does not say. Section 6.7 adds one more thing the mathematics does not say: that embedding a model of harm makes its use for avoidance hard to invert.

What did not change.

No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proof or identity of version 1.3 was altered, except Proposition V-4, its proof and the passage of Section 7.3 named above; no quotation of the registration was changed, and the frozen registration texts are untouched.

Checked for this version.

Every changed or new derivation was worked through again and checked on synthetic numbers by a script that imports no study code and reads no data; every quotation new to this version was compared with its source by code.

B.2 Version 1.3, 17 November 2026

Version 1.3 is the report’s next version. It follows version 1.2 of 29 October 2026, which stays published as revision 2 of the report’s PDF on OSF.

Why it was made.

A second derivation of every result of version 1.2, made within the programme on 17 November 2026, found no definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proposition, proof or identity of version 1.2 wrong. Version 1.3 adds hypotheses that version 1.2 left unstated, the scope of Theorems IV-G and IV-H, a minimal training model for Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, and two minimal models for Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, each UNREGISTERED.

What changed.

  1. Hypotheses stated. Lemma IV-K’s premise is any set of finite paths (Section 5.3); the kernel of a set of paths without the length-zero path, and the kernel at horizon zero, are stated (Section 5.2); a positive infimum differs from pointwise positivity only over infinitely many exits (Section 5.4); Corollary IV-H′' starts from a state in ΩV\Omega_V (Section 5.5); the constant two of Proposition IV-N cannot be lowered (Section 5.5.1); the reading rule is invariant under increasing affine changes, with the floor on the battery’s own scale (Section 5.6); the floor gives the gate only on an interval whose critical value is at least the gate’s (Section 5.6.1); and the boundary reading holds for changes that keep κ−χ\kappa - \chi of one sign (Section 6.1).

  2. Scope. Theorems IV-G and IV-H do not reach later training by gradient steps (Section 5.7); a concurrent-baseline retained fraction reads a property the later objective holds as a gain lost (Section 5.6); a dilution common to both arms shrinks the difference and leaves ΛV\Lambda_V unchanged (Section 9); the registration’s two statements of the build-order limb’s refutation differ on some intervals (Section 6.6, item 2, and Section 10, item 15); on the counted instrument for P21 the route of recursion as such is absent by design (Section 6.5); equation (22) reads χ\chi as an elasticity of correction capacity (Section 7.6); and the third of Section 1’s plain terms names the two quantities that move the balance root, a correction the conclusion carries too.

  3. Two sections, each UNREGISTERED. Section 5.9, a minimal training model; and Section 6.8, two minimal models for Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, with a sentence in Section 6.1 on the premise the build-order limb carries. The proofs are in Appendix A.

  4. A second reading of the three models, made within the programme before this version was set, changed five things: the placement model’s widening is stated on the ratio from depth one and on the difference only beyond a turning depth, with a worked example; the statement that a widening has two routes names its two premises and gives the extra terms where either fails; the build-order model’s co-scaling premise is given its range of capability, and its two-rung interval is closed; its cancellation premise is stated as a premise, with what an instrument does to keep it; and the statement for equal detection takes the increment formula as its reason. It also supplied the short proof of Corollary IV-C′'.

  5. Status. The status of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, is printed in its signed form, with the unit, its registration date, its run dates and its DOIs in a sentence of their own, and with the limbs that can and cannot yet be decided (Section 11).

  6. The value two. Where the value two is quoted, the section says that it is the relative rung’s value, and Section 7.4 states once what the absolute rung asks, as the registration’s entry for P3 requires.

  7. Related work and the search. Section 2 adds the training model’s credits, the two works of 2026 nearest to Theorem IV-C, the earlier statement in words of three ideas the laws state in measurable form, and what a search of 17 November 2026 found for the two models of Law V, the ARC Embedding Law: twenty-two queries in two families, half of them for the opposite, on OpenAlex and the web (arXiv’s query interface refused automated requests that day), with twelve works read at their official records, each at its abstract. It found earlier statements bearing on both models’ premises, for and against, and did not find either model’s results stated in what was read. The sentence after the contributions, Section 11’s sentence on what the report supplies and the limitation on earlier work now say what Section 2 names and where each search’s date and scope stand, in place of a disclaimer of novelty.

  8. Law names. Each law named by its number carries its registered name at that mention, through the whole text.

  9. The first page. The plate says what the mathematics now is and how many of the fifteen questions the registration has settled; the plate and the Introduction say of the Eden Protocol what Section 8 says, that it is a method, not a law, and is not entailed by these laws; the abstract carries the three developments; and the abstract and the Introduction each open with the report’s own questions, in words no other paper of the programme prints.

  10. Corrections. The first page’s author line now names the author’s page and his book only; the title now carries the report’s established name before its question; Paper X’s reference gives the title its PDF prints; and wherever the report gives a registered rule’s words it now cites them where version 1.104 states them, while a dated event, such as what version 1.103 registered on 15 October 2026, keeps version 1.103.

  11. Said once. Three places in Sections 5.9 and 6.8 that made one point twice now make it once: the plain reading of Theorem IV-C says once that the embedded weights can change sign; the moderator sentence names the change of capability domain without restating the embedded advantage; and the sentence on the turning depth no longer repeats the conditions of Proposition V-4(c).

What did not change.

No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proposition, proof or identity of version 1.2 was altered, except where item 1 adds a hypothesis, a range or a scope sentence; no quotation of the registration was changed, and the frozen registration is untouched.

Checked for this version.

Every result new to this version was derived twice within the programme and checked on synthetic numbers by a script that imports no study code and reads no data; every quotation new to this version was compared with its source, and each work’s official address was read on 17 November 2026.

B.3 Version 1.2, 29 October 2026

Version 1.2 is the report’s next version. It follows version 1.1, frozen on 7 October 2026 and published on 12 October 2026, which stays published as revision 3 of the same file on OSF.

Why it was made.

Version 1.103 of the theory registration, registered on 15 October 2026, registers Laws IV and V as laws and says of this report: “Where this text and that report differ, this text governs how the laws take their words, and the report’s next version restates the sentences concerned.” (registration version 1.103, the paragraph on the mathematics and where the successor departs from its report). Version 1.2 is that next version.

What changed.

  1. The laws’ standing. Version 1.1 said that neither law was yet registered as a law; that was true on its date and is not now. The laws are stated throughout as version 1.103 registers them: added on 24 September 2026, registered as laws on 15 October 2026, each a law under test, with the status of the first registered test of one of their propositions (Section 11), which also names, once, the programme’s first registered study, Unit 06, which tests no law.

  2. The three places version 1.103 departs from version 1.1, each restated in the registered form, with the version 1.1 wording kept in Appendix B.4. Law IV has two limbs, the retention limb, P15’s registered claim word for word, and a comparison limb with no registered proposition yet (Sections 5.1 and 5.8). Law V’s build-order limb has a direction, the genesis reading of version 1.1, read on P12’s interval while P12 keeps no direction (Sections 6.1 and 6.6). And Law V’s dependence on Law IV is narrower: it is struck only by a refuted verdict on Law IV’s comparison limb, so that a refuted P15 alone leaves Law V to its own limbs (Section 8, item 3). With them the laws’ verdict rules, the open questions version 1.103 settled and the register of unregistered objects are restated (Sections 5.8, 6.6, 9 and 10).

  3. Version 1.104, approved on 29 October 2026. The regression re-estimate of approximately 0.49 is no longer called robust, since it is one model’s fit (Section 7.6), and version 1.104’s readings of P15’s decision requirement are quoted where P15’s kill condition stands (Section 5.8).

  4. The status label. The label PROPOSED, which versions 0.2.1 to 1.1 gave the objects this document states beyond the registration, is written UNREGISTERED, and the conventions of earlier versions are described as set out; the meaning is unchanged: none is law content until the author registers it.

  5. The first-publication label. Version 1.1 printed “First published 12 October 2026”, the date on which version 1.1 was published. The report’s earliest public version, working draft 0.2.1, is dated 1 October 2026 inside the document, and the report was first deposited on OSF on 3 October 2026, as working draft 0.2.4 (Table 6 and Appendix C).

  6. The register sentence. The statement paper’s register sentence for ARC-4 (Eastwood 2026h) is labelled as the register’s, and the laws’ statements printed are version 1.103’s (Section 5.6).

  7. Links. Every mention of the registration, the statement paper and the programme’s papers links its OSF DOI; the programme’s notation links its register of operational definitions; the author’s working paper of 16 August 2026 has no official online source, and says so.

  8. The presentation standard. The report is set in LaTeX on the programme’s template, with a title block, an abstract, a contents page, an introduction with its contributions, a related-work section whose works were each read at their official sources on 29 October 2026, a section on what the report does and does not show, its limitations and a conclusion. The proofs move to Appendix A, the symbol list to Appendix D, the dating to Appendix C and the records of version 1.1 to this appendix; Table 5 maps the section numbers. One figure draws the example retention curve of Section 5.6. The author block takes the template’s form.

  9. The source of two quotations. Version 1.1 quoted the one-line statement of each law from the author’s statement of the laws, which no programme paper prints; this version gives those lines in its own words (Sections 5.1 and 6.1), and Appendix B.4 keeps version 1.1’s sentences.

What did not change.

No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proposition, assumption, proof, identity, equation, number, interval rule or quotation of version 1.102 was altered, and no mathematical object, result or prediction was added; the registered words the laws now take are quoted from version 1.103, and each place where version 1.103 changes how a law takes its words is listed in Appendix B.4.

Checked for this version.

Every equation, theorem statement, number, date and DOI of version 1.1 was mapped by script to its place in this edition; every quotation new in this version was compared with its source, those of versions 1.103 and 1.104 with their approved texts; and the identity of each linked address was confirmed at the registry or publisher that issues it on 29 October 2026.

B.5 The records of version 1.1

Version 1.1, frozen on 7 October 2026. It follows version 1.0 of 3 October 2026, which stays as published; section 9 lists what changed and what was checked. A later version is a new text under a new number.

What this version adds to version 0.2.1.

Version 1.0 froze the working draft 0.2.4 and added no object to it: it closed one case of Proposition IV-R, named the terms of one model in section 3.4 and reworded one clause of section 2.8. This version adds no object either. The additions are those of the working draft, four of them PROPOSED: a planner that scores its plans with bounded error (section 2.5.1); the baseline, the arms and the interval that the retained fraction needs before it can be read (section 2.6.1); the balance over a finite range of depth (section 4.8); and what a new deciding instrument declares before its outcomes are read (section 4.9). It also takes out of force the law-level conventions that version 0.2.1 proposed as defaults, and keeps them on the record as proposals (sections 2.8, 3.6, 5 and 7). A PROPOSED rule is never a registered decision rule. Section 9 says what was checked for this version and what remains open.

B.5.1 Checks of version 1.1

Every identity and derivation in this document was checked by computer algebra. The proofs of its theorems, lemmas and propositions are written proofs, which finite models exercise and do not replace. Every quotation was compared, byte for byte, with its source, which is the frozen text of registration version 1.102, the statement paper at version 6.7 or the author’s statement of the laws, and the identity of each address to which this document links was confirmed at the registry that issues it, on 3 October 2026 for version 1.0 and on 7 October 2026 for this version.

Corrections to version 0.2.1, dated 3 October 2026.

Section 3.4: the example of an arm that doubles service while halving attained capability holds at unit elasticity only, and now says so. Section 5 item 2: the registered dials do not by themselves make Laws I to III hold, and the text now says what the dials do show. Section 6: the difference of the two retained fractions is defined only where both are established, not always. Section 2.8 item 1: that the baseline convention be fixed in advance is this document’s PROPOSED requirement and no part of P15’s registered face.

Changes from the working draft 0.2.4, dated 3 October 2026.

The label, the title and the front matter say what this version is. Section 0: the sources paragraph records that the sentences quoted from the statement paper stand unchanged in its version 7.0 and links the paper’s title to its DOI address; the status lines say what this version sets out and name the proved results as the text names them; the description of what this document is not says that it adds no registered proposition. Section 1: the reference value of service is defined in words. Section 2.6: Fieller (1954)’s method carries its reference. Section 2.6.1: the account of where Proposition IV-R stops now covers the case of equality and the case of a negative denominator, and calls the unbounded set what it is. Section 2.8 item 5: its second sentence now opens on a condition, because no withdrawal convention is in force. Section 3.4 names the six fixed terms the smaller model keeps. Section 8 dates the working draft and this version and calls version 0.2.1 the earlier working draft. This section lists these changes, states the second check and says how the linked addresses were confirmed. Every mention of the registration, of the statement paper and of Paper VIII outside a quotation is linked to its DOI address, and Fieller (1954)’s method to its source. No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, identity or proposition was altered.

The second check.

The working draft was checked a second time from its text alone, by code that shared nothing with the first check: exact rational arithmetic for every printed number, and searches over small finite models for the written proofs. Fifty checks ran and fifty passed. The two cases added to section 2.6.1 in this version were checked in exact arithmetic over random cases before the version was frozen.

Changes from version 1.0, dated 7 October 2026.

Laws IV and V are no longer called candidates, and neither is this document. Section 0 states the laws’ standing in full (added on 24 September 2026; their propositions registered; neither law yet registered as a law or tested; their mathematics set out here), and what this document is opens on their mathematics; in the front matter, the three levels name the two laws as empirical claims. Sections 2.1 and 3.1 are headed Statement, and the tag before each statement carries the same standing in short form. Where sections 2.1, 2.6 and 2.8, the row for IV-PERSIST in section 6 and item 1 of section 7 said what this document’s formulation does, they now say it of this version, or here. The word candidate stays where it grades neither the laws nor this document: the candidate descriptive families and the outcome NO CANDIDATE FITS (section 2.6), the candidate retention families (section 6), the candidate mixed model (section 3.4), and objects that are candidates for a registration of their own (sections 4.9 and 6). The title now follows the programme’s uniform order (paper, its law or framework, its own title); until this version it read “Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.0”. The label carries version 1.1, and the front matter prints this document’s DOI. The front matter and section 8 name version 1.0 where they called it this version, and the first paragraph of this section dates the confirmation of the linked addresses for each version. The entries above dated 3 October 2026, and the second check, record version 1.0 and stand as written: where they say this version, they mean version 1.0. No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proposition, assumption, proof, identity, equation, number, interval rule, open question, registered wording or quotation was changed, and no object, claim or prediction was added. For this version the computer-algebra checks were run again on its text, and every quotation was compared again with its source.

These checks are the programme’s own. They are not independent verification, no proof assistant was used, and nothing here is an empirical result. This version is frozen: a later version is a new text under a new number, with its changes listed.

B.5.2 Changes in version 1.1

Michael Darius Eastwood. 7 October 2026.

Version 1.1 is frozen. This list compares it with version 1.0 of 3 October 2026, which stays as published. Nothing in this list is a registration or an empirical result.

From version 1.0 to version 1.1.

Only words change. No definition, lemma, theorem, corollary, proposition, assumption, proof, identity, equation, number, interval rule, open question, registered wording or quotation is altered, and no object, claim or prediction is added.

  • Laws IV and V are no longer called candidates, and neither is this document. Their standing is stated in full: added on 24 September 2026; their propositions registered (P15 in register ARC-4; P12 and P21 in register ARC-5); neither law yet registered as a law or tested; their mathematics set out in this document, now at version 1.1.

  • Section 0, the status line: it states that standing, and it folds in what each law carries, so that nothing is said twice. What this document is: the mathematics of Law IV and of Law V.

  • The front matter, the three levels: the second level is the two laws as empirical claims.

  • Sections 2.1 and 3.1 are headed “Statement”, and the tag before each statement carries the standing in short form: for Law IV “added 24 September 2026; its proposition, P15, registered in ARC-4; not yet registered as a law or tested”, and for Law V “added 24 September 2026; its propositions, P12 and P21, registered in ARC-5; not yet registered as a law or tested”.

  • Where the text said what this document’s formulation does or adopts (sections 2.1, 2.6 and 2.8, the row for IV-PERSIST in section 6, and section 7 item 1), it now says “this version”, or “here” for the default baseline of section 2.6.

  • The title follows the programme’s uniform order (paper, its law or framework, its own title): “Report · The ARC Theory · Laws IV and V, the ARC Persistence Law and the ARC Embedding Law · The Mathematics”. Until this version it read “Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.0”, which stays the title of version 1.0.

  • The label: version 1.1, frozen on 7 October 2026, following version 1.0. The front matter prints this document’s DOI, 10.17605/OSF.IO/4B3VT, and says that this version adds no object; it and section 8 name version 1.0 where they called it this version.

  • Section 9: the first paragraph dates the confirmation of the linked addresses for each version, and a new entry lists these changes. The entries dated 3 October 2026, and the second check, stand as written; in them, “this version” means version 1.0.

Where the word candidate stays.

It stays where it grades neither the laws nor this document.

  • “Candidate descriptive families” and the outcome “NO CANDIDATE FITS” (section 2.6), and “the candidate retention families” (section 6): a closed set of descriptive model families fixed before any deciding run, none of which is the law, and the outcome in which none of them fits.

  • “a candidate mixed model” (section 3.4): one model of the closed model set.

  • “a candidate for a registration of its own” (section 4.9) and “candidates for a registration of their own” (section 6): objects the author may register in their own right.

Unchanged.

  • The register assignment of section 0.1 and every registration line number.

  • The fifteen open questions of section 7 and their defaults. Items 2, 3 and 4 name no default: those decisions are the author’s.
